_**User (2026-10-03 20:13:11Z)**_

Here is issue 45. I want a fully realized solution for it and then to implement once design designs are made and reviewed by me. # Issue Description

## Summary

Allow users to define a path that an element can follow.

This should support creating paths using coordinates or points and provide a way to edit the path after it has been created. The path should be associated with a selected element or group of elements.

## User Story

**As a** team lead or designer, **I want** to be able to animate elements along paths **so that** I can better convey and visualize my ideas to my team.

## User Scenario

1. Go to Path Tool on HUD Bar.
2. Click an element on canvas
3. Draw a path with start, end, and (optional) midpoints
4. Confirm path.
5. Click and Hold element for a second, the animation plays afterwards.

---

# Issue Classification

## Scope

**Generic:** Medium **Specific:** Greater Medium (8 points) **Reason:** Core motion-path system requiring path creation, configuration, and integration with elements.

---

# Expectations

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Create Path:** Users can create a motion path using a line and points.
- [ ] **Path with Multiple Points:** Users can create paths containing multiple points.
- [ ] **Retain Path Points:** Path points retain their configured positions after the path is created.
- [ ] **Follow Path:** An element follows its assigned path when the animation is played.
- [ ] **Multiple Path:** Multiple elements can have independently assigned motion paths (2+ path exist at once).

## Open Question

**N/A**

---

# Extra

## Out of Scope

- Adds movement behavior, coordinates, speed, and timing to elements.
- Requires animation state, playback controls, timing, and movement execution.
- Adds editing of paths and associated elements without replacing the core motion system.
- Requires motion data to survive save/reopen and work with presentation behavior.

## Head Issue

Issue (#18): Allow elements to have motion

---

2. How is the "line" tool implemented end-to-end — from click in toolbar, to pointer-down/pointer-move/pointer-up handlers in the canvas, to creation of a multi-point linear element (like in packages/excalidraw/element or App.tsx)? 174	export const findShapeByKey = (key: string, app: AppClassProperties) => {
175	  // CapsLock-insensitive (the caller excludes modified keypresses, incl.
176	  // shift, so a capital letter here means CapsLock)
177	  const lowerKey = key.toLowerCase();
178
179	  for (const type of Object.keys(TOOLS) as ToolbarToolType[]) {
180	    const { letterKey, numericKey } = TOOLS[type];
181	    if (
182	      (numericKey != null && key === numericKey) ||
183	      (letterKey &&
184	        (typeof letterKey === "string"
185	          ? letterKey === lowerKey
186	          : letterKey.includes(lowerKey)))
187	    ) {
188	      // the selection shortcut activates whichever selection tool the user
189	      // prefers (selection or lasso)
190	      return type === "selection"
191	        ? app.state.preferredSelectionTool.type

193	    }
194	  }
195	  return null;
196	};

210	type ToolButtonBehavior = {

214	   * when lasso is the preferred selection tool

227	/**
228	 * Creates a toolbar button component for the given tool. Activation is
229	 * uniform: track + `setActiveTool` (recording the previous tool for toggle
230	 * tools), with pen detection on the first pen interaction.
231	 */
232	const createToolButton = (
233	  type: ToolbarToolType,
234	  behavior?: ToolButtonBehavior,
235	) => {
236	  const config = TOOLS[type];
237	  const shortcutType = behavior?.shortcutType ?? type;
238
239	  const ToolButtonComponent = ({
240	    app,
241	    activeTool,
242	    hideKeyBinding,
243	    hideShortcut,
244	  }: ToolButtonComponentProps) => {
245	    const label = capitalizeString(t(`toolBar.${type}`));
246	    const shortcut = hideShortcut ? null : getToolShortcut(shortcutType);
247
248	    return (
249	      <IconButton
250	        className={clsx({ fillable: config.fillable })}
251	        type="toggle"
252	        icon={config.icon}
253	        checked={activeTool.type === type}
254	        title={shortcut ? `${label} — ${shortcut}` : label}
255	        keyBindingLabel={
256	          hideKeyBinding || hideShortcut
257	            ? undefined
258	            : TOOLS[shortcutType].numericKey || getToolLetter(shortcutType)
259	        }
260	        aria-label={label}
261	        aria-keyshortcuts={shortcut ?? undefined}
262	        data-testid={`toolbar-${type}`}
263	        onSelect={({ pointerType }) => {
264	          if (!app.state.penDetected && pointerType === "pen") {
265	            app.togglePenMode(true);
266	          }
267
268	          if (behavior?.onSelect) {
269	            behavior.onSelect(app, { pointerType });
270	            return;
271	          }
272
273	          if (app.state.activeTool.type !== type) {
274	            trackEvent("toolbar", type, "ui");
275	            app.setActiveTool({ type });
276	          }
277	        }}
278	      />
279	    );
280	  };
281
282	  ToolButtonComponent.displayName = `${capitalizeString(type)}IconButton`;
283
284	  return ToolButtonComponent;
285	};

69	/**
70	 * Single source of truth for "which shape-action controls are relevant right
71	 * now". Each flag answers whether a given control should be shown, given the
72	 * active tool and the current selection. All three styles-panel layouts
73	 * (full / compact / mobile) and the compact popovers consume these flags so
74	 * that visibility logic lives in one place and layout stays pure.
75	 */
76	export const getShapeActionPredicates = (
77	  appState: UIAppState,
78	  targetElements: ExcalidrawElement[],
79	  elementsMap: NonDeletedElementsMap | NonDeletedSceneElementsMap,
80	  app: AppClassProperties,
81	) => {
82	  const activeToolType = appState.activeTool.type;
83
84	  // A property is relevant when it applies to the active tool (so it can be
85	  // preconfigured before drawing) or to any currently selected element.
86	  const forToolOrSelection = (
87	    predicate: (type: ElementOrToolType) => boolean,
88	  ) =>
89	    predicate(activeToolType) ||
90	    targetElements.some((element) => predicate(element.type));
91
92	  const singleSelected = targetElements.length === 1;
93
94	  // a container + its bound text read as a single logical element (2 selected)
95	  const isSingleElementBoundContainer =
96	    targetElements.length === 2 &&
97	    (hasBoundTextElement(targetElements[0]) ||
98	      hasBoundTextElement(targetElements[1]));
99
100	  const isEditingTextOrNewElement = Boolean(
101	    appState.editingTextElement || appState.newElement,
102	  );
103	  const hasSelection = targetElements.length > 0;
104
105	  return {
106	    /** some element(s) selected */
107	    hasSelection,
108	    /** actions on selected elements (delete/duplicate/...) */
109	    showExtraActions: hasSelection && !isEditingTextOrNewElement,
110
111	    // color
112	    strokeColor: canChangeStrokeColor(appState, targetElements),
113	    backgroundColor: canChangeBackgroundColor(appState, targetElements),
114	    fill:
115	      (hasBackground(activeToolType) &&
116	        !isTransparent(appState.currentItemBackgroundColor)) ||
117	      targetElements.some(
118	        (element) =>
119	          hasBackground(element.type) &&
120	          !isTransparent(element.backgroundColor),
121	      ),
122
123	    // stroke / shape properties
124	    strokeWidth: forToolOrSelection(hasStrokeWidth),
125	    freedrawMode: forToolOrSelection(hasFreedrawMode),
126	    strokeStyle: forToolOrSelection(hasStrokeStyle),
127	    roundness: forToolOrSelection(canChangeRoundness),
128	    arrowType: forToolOrSelection(toolIsArrow),
129	    arrowheads: forToolOrSelection(canHaveArrowheads),
130
131	    // text
132	    text: activeToolType === "text" || targetElements.some(isTextElement),
133	    textAlign:
134	      activeToolType === "text" ||
135	      suppportsHorizontalAlign(targetElements, elementsMap),
136	    verticalAlign: shouldAllowVerticalAlign(targetElements, elementsMap),
137
138	    // arrangement
139	    align:
140	      !isSingleElementBoundContainer && alignActionsPredicate(appState, app),
141	    distribute: targetElements.length > 2,
142
143	    // per-element actions
144	    // NOTE: the full panel treats a bound container as linkable; the compact /
145	    // mobile layouts only link a truly single selection. Both are preserved via
146	    // the two flags below.
147	    link: singleSelected || isSingleElementBoundContainer,
148	    linkSingleOnly: singleSelected,
149	    cropEditor:
150	      !appState.croppingElementId &&
151	      singleSelected &&
152	      isImageElement(targetElements[0]),
153	    lineEditor:

155	      singleSelected &&
156	      isLinearElement(targetElements[0]) &&
157	      !isElbowArrow(targetElements[0]),
158	  };
159	};

## Findings

### 1. Element discriminated union (`packages/element/src/types.ts`)

Base props in `_ExcalidrawElementBase` (types.ts:40-82): `id, x, y, strokeColor, backgroundColor, fillStyle, strokeWidth, strokeStyle, roundness, roughness, opacity, width, height, angle, seed, version, versionNonce, index (FractionalIndex), isDeleted, groupIds: readonly GroupId[], frameId: string | null, boundElements: readonly BoundElement[] | null, updated, link, locked, customData?`.

`ExcalidrawGenericElement` (types.ts:184-189) = selection/rectangle/diamond/ellipse/triangle (base + just `type`).

`ExcalidrawElement` top-level union (types.ts:211-221): `ExcalidrawGenericElement | ExcalidrawTextElement | ExcalidrawLinearElement | ExcalidrawArrowElement | ExcalidrawFreeDrawElement | ExcalidrawImageElement | ExcalidrawFrameElement | ExcalidrawMagicFrameElement | ExcalidrawIframeElement | ExcalidrawEmbeddableElement`. Discrimination is via literal `type: "rectangle" | "line" | ...` on each member.

`ExcalidrawLinearElement` (types.ts:340-348):

```ts
export type ExcalidrawLinearElement = _ExcalidrawElementBase &
  Readonly<{
    type: "line" | "arrow";
    points: readonly LocalPoint[];
    startBinding: FixedPointBinding | null;
    endBinding: FixedPointBinding | null;
    startArrowhead: Arrowhead | null;
    endArrowhead: Arrowhead | null;
  }>;
```

`ExcalidrawArrowElement` adds `elbowed: boolean` (types.ts:362-366). `FixedPointBinding` (types.ts:291-300) = `{ elementId, fixedPoint: [number, number] }` — binds to a single `ExcalidrawBindableElement["id"]`.

Note: `lastCommittedPoint` is **not** on the element itself — it lives on the ephemeral editor class `LinearElementEditor` (`packages/element/src/linearElementEditor.ts:149,182`), used only while actively drawing/editing a multi-point line, and referenced from `appState.selectedLinearElement` (see `App.tsx:7433-7508`). This is the right model to mimic for an in-progress motion-path edit.

### 2. Validation/restore and the "all types" enumeration

- Canonical exhaustive type list: `isExcalidrawElement` in `packages/element/src/typeChecks.ts:246-275` — a `switch(type)` over all 13 types ending in `default: assertNever(type, null)`. **Adding a new type requires a case here or TS will fail the exhaustiveness check.**
- `packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts:506` — `restoreElement`'s switch handles `text/freedraw/image/line/arrow/embeddable/frame/...` per-type normalization (lines 557-699+).
- `packages/element/src/renderElement.ts` has three separate type switches: line 94 (path generation), line 324 (roundness/shape-specific), line 738 (draw-to-canvas dispatch, with `case "freedraw"` at 782, rectanguloid cases at 817-826).
- `packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts` also matched `"rectangle"` etc. in the earlier grep — SVG export has its own per-type branch.

These are the touchpoints to flag (not implement) for future persistence/render work.

### 3. Binding (`packages/element/src/binding.ts`)

- Binding is **element-to-element only**, never group-level. `startBinding`/`endBinding` each hold one `elementId: ExcalidrawBindableElement["id"]` (types.ts:291-300). `ExcalidrawBindableElement` (types.ts:264-274) = rectangle/diamond/triangle/ellipse/text/image/iframe/embeddable/frame/magicframe.
- `isArrowBoundToElement` (typeChecks.ts:308-310) just checks truthiness of start/endBinding.
- No group-aware binding path exists in binding.ts — binding logic (`bindableElementsVisitor`, hit-testing around lines 363-765) always resolves to a single bindable element id, even when that element belongs to a group (`groupIds` is irrelevant to binding resolution).

### 4. Groups & selection

- `groupIds: readonly GroupId[]` on every element (types.ts:73), ordered deepest→shallowest. `selectGroup` (`packages/element/src/groups.ts:24-60`) expands a groupId into membership by scanning `element.groupIds.includes(groupId)`.
- `getSelectedElements` (`packages/element/src/selection.ts:161-193`) is the resolver for "selected element(s)": iterates elements, includes any whose `id` is in `appState.selectedElementIds` (a `{[id]: true}` map), with opt-in flags `includeBoundTextElement` (also includes text via `containerId` match, line 184-192) and `includeElementsInFrames`. Group selection is represented as **multiple individual selectedElementIds** that happen to share a groupId, not a distinct group entity — so "bind to a group" in practice means "bind to N member elements," or you'd need a new association field holding a `GroupId` and resolve membership via `groupIds.includes()` at use time, consistent with how `selectGroup` does it.

### 5. "Owned-by-another-element" pattern precedents

Two existing patterns worth copying:

- **containerId** (text→shape): `ExcalidrawTextElement.containerId: ExcalidrawGenericElement["id"] | null` (types.ts:248); reverse link via `boundElements: BoundElement[]` on the container (types.ts:35-38, 76). Checked via `isBoundToContainer`/`hasBoundTextElement` (typeChecks.ts:287-306).
- **frameId** (child→frame): plain `frameId: string | null` on `_ExcalidrawElementBase` (types.ts:74), resolved via `getFrameChildren`/`isFrameLikeElement` (seen in selection.ts:196-201), no reverse array needed since frame membership is computed by scanning all elements' `frameId`.

For a motion path, the `containerId`-style explicit FK field (e.g. `associatedElementId: string | null`) plus optional reverse-registration in `boundElements` (new `BoundElement` type entry, currently `type: "arrow" | "text"` at types.ts:37) is the most consistent pattern; `frameId`-style (scan-based, no reverse pointer) is simpler if two-way lookup isn't needed.

Group selection is represented as **multiple individual selectedElementIds** that happen to share a groupId, not a distinct group entity — so "bind to a group" in practice means "bind to N member elements," or you'd need a new association field holding a `GroupId` and resolve membership via `groupIds.includes()` at use time, consistent with how `selectGroup` does it.

### 5. "Owned-by-another-element" pattern precedents

Two existing patterns worth copying:

- **containerId** (text→shape): `ExcalidrawTextElement.containerId: ExcalidrawGenericElement["id"] | null` (types.ts:248); reverse link via `boundElements: BoundElement[]` on the container (types.ts:35-38, 76). Checked via `isBoundToContainer`/`hasBoundTextElement` (typeChecks.ts:287-306).
- **frameId** (child→frame): plain `frameId: string | null` on `_ExcalidrawElementBase` (types.ts:74), resolved via `getFrameChildren`/`isFrameLikeElement` (seen in selection.ts:196-201), no reverse array needed since frame membership is computed by scanning all elements' `frameId`.

For a motion path, the `containerId`-style explicit FK field (e.g. `associatedElementId: string | null`) plus optional reverse-registration in `boundElements` (new `BoundElement` type entry, currently `type: "arrow" | "text"` at types.ts:37) is the most consistent pattern; `frameId`-style (scan-based, no reverse pointer) is simpler if two-way lookup isn't needed.</result> <usage><subagent_tokens>45763</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>24</tool_uses><duration_ms>73871</duration_ms></usage> </task-notification>

### 1. Toolbar/tool registry

- `findShapeByKey()` (`Tools.tsx:174-196`) resolves a keypress to a tool type — this is what you'd extend for a new shortcut.
- `createToolButton()` (`Tools.tsx:232-285`) factory builds each `*ToolButton` component (`LineToolButton` etc. at `Tools.tsx:287-298`), calling `app.setActiveTool({ type })`.
- Toolbar composition (which buttons actually render, in what order) is in **`packages/excalidraw/components/Toolbar.tsx:225-242`** (main row) and `ExtraToolsDropdown` (`Toolbar.tsx:49-164`) for overflow tools (frame, embeddable, laser, lasso) — a new "Path" tool not fitting the main row would go in the dropdown like `frame`/`embeddable`.
- Icons live in `packages/excalidraw/components/icons.tsx` (imported at `Tools.tsx:12-29`, e.g. `LineIcon`).
- `ToolType` union: **`packages/excalidraw/types.ts:145-162`**; `ElementOrToolType`/`ActiveTool` at `types.ts:164+`.

### 2. Line tool end-to-end

- Click dispatch: `App.tsx` pointer-down branch at **`App.tsx:8358-8366`**: `activeTool.type === "arrow" || "line"` → `handleLinearElementOnPointerDown(event, type, pointerDownState)`.
- `handleLinearElementOnPointerDown` (**`App.tsx:9511+`**): if `this.state.multiElement` is set, each click either adds a point or finalizes (loop detection via `isPathALoop`, or click-within `LINE_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD` of `lastCommittedPoint`, `App.tsx:9532-9629`) by calling `this.actionManager.executeAction(actionFinalize, ...)`. First click creates the element via `newLinearElement` and sets `appState.multiElement`/`newElement`.
- Pointer-move while drawing: `App.tsx:1079-1087` / `7540` — branches on `this.state.multiElement` to call `LinearElementEditor.handlePointerMove` (multi-point mode) vs `LinearElementEditor.handlePointDragging` (drag-to-draw single segment).
- Finalize triggers: double-click-in-commit-zone, Enter, or Escape — Escape/Enter handling in `App.tsx` keydown around **`App.tsx:2079`, `5117`, `5139`** and the dedicated `onKeyDownFromPointerDownHandler`; all route to **`packages/excalidraw/actions/actionFinalize.tsx`** (registered `name: "finalize"`, `actionFinalize.tsx:53+`), which commits points, unbinds/binds, trims invisible elements, and clears `multiElement`/`selectedLinearElement`.
- Element construction: `newLinearElement` / `newArrowElement` in **`packages/element/src/newElement.ts:467-494` / `496+`** — builds `{ type, points: [], startBinding, endBinding, startArrowhead, endArrowhead }`, and wraps as `ExcalidrawLineElement` with `polygon` flag if `isLineElement`.

### 3. `activeTool` dispatch in App.tsx

- Main per-tool pointer-down branch: **`App.tsx:8356-8397`** (`text` → `handleTextOnPointerDown`; `arrow`/`line` → `handleLinearElementOnPointerDown`; `freedraw` → `handleFreeDrawElementOnPointerDown`; `custom` → generic cursor only; `frame`/`magicframe` → `createFrameElementOnPointerDown`; `laser` → laser trail; else → `createGenericElementOnPointerDown`). This is the branch point to add a new `"path"` case.

### 4. Editing points after creation — `LinearElementEditor`

- **`packages/element/src/linearElementEditor.ts`**, class `LinearElementEditor` (line 125): `handlePointerDown` (1021), `handlePointerMove` (291, used during initial multi-point draw), `handlePointerMoveInEditMode` (1189, used when re-editing an existing line's points), `handlePointerUp` (693), `getPointIndexUnderCursor` (1351), `addMidpoint` (1699, double-click on a segment to insert a point).
- `appState.selectedLinearElement` holds editor state (`isEditing`, `lastCommittedPoint`, `selectedPointsIndices`, `pointerDownState` etc.); entering edit mode happens via `actionToggleLinearEditor` (referenced `App.tsx:5452`) on Enter/double-click of a selected line/arrow.

## Findings

**1. Selection-dependent panel pattern** — `packages/excalidraw/components/Actions.tsx:136-215` (`SelectedShapeActions`) computes `targetElements = getTargetElements(elementsMap, appState)` (`packages/element/src/selection.ts:214-227`, flattens selection to actual elements, including bound text) then calls `getShapeActionPredicates()` (`packages/excalidraw/components/shapeActionPredicates.ts:76-159`). Key flags to copy:

- `singleSelected = targetElements.length === 1` (line 92)
- `hasSelection = targetElements.length > 0` (line 103)
- Per-control predicates like `cropEditor`/`lineEditor` gate on `singleSelected && isImageElement(targetElements[0])` (lines 149-157) — this is the exact template for "render extra UI only when exactly one element selected."
- JSX conditionally renders: `{predicates.cropEditor && renderAction("cropEditor")}` (Actions.tsx:208).

**2. Action registration conditioned on selection** — `packages/excalidraw/actions/actionGroup.tsx`. `actionGroup` (lines 86-212) has a `predicate: (elements, appState, _, app) => enableActionGroup(...)` (line 197-198) where `enableActionGroup` (lines 69-84) requires `selectedElements.length >= 2 && !allElementsInSameGroup(...)`. `actionUngroup`'s predicate is `getSelectedGroupIds(appState).length > 0` (line 307). Each action also has a `PanelComponent` using `hidden={!enableActionGroup(...)}` (line 203) / `visible={isSomeElementSelected(...)}` (line 209/317) — this `predicate` + `PanelComponent` pair, registered via `register()` (`packages/excalidraw/actions/register.ts`), is the model for a "Create Motion Path" action enabled only when exactly one element/group is selected.

**3. Multi-step "confirm" flow (`multiElement`)** — `appState.multiElement` in `packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx` holds the in-progress linear element while drawing a multi-point line (set at e.g. line 11241 `multiElement: newElement`, cleared to `null` at finalize, e.g. lines 5813, 5824, 6599, 9898, 9932). `actionFinalize` (`packages/excalidraw/actions/actionFinalize.tsx`):

- `keyTest` at lines 397-400: fires on `ESCAPE` (while editing linear element) or `ESCAPE`/`ENTER` when `appState.multiElement !== null`.
- `perform()` (lines 57-396) validates/commits the element (closes loop if `isPathALoop`, line 290; converts to `polygon` if valid, line 300-316), resets `multiElement: null`, `newElement: null`, sets `selectedElementIds` to the finished element, and resets the active tool (unless locked).
- `PanelComponent` (lines 401-412) renders a "Done" `IconButton` with `visible={appState.multiElement != null}` — directly reusable pattern for a path-tool "Confirm" button.
- App.tsx double-click / pointerup handling around lines 7428-7531 and 9524-9636 shows how new points get appended to `multiElement.points` and how binding/midpoint logic integrates — relevant if the path tool needs midpoints bound to the target element.

**4. Toolbar button + tooltip + shortcut badge** — `packages/excalidraw/components/Tools.tsx`. `TOOLS` registry (lines 63-145) is the single source of truth: `{ icon, letterKey, numericKey, fillable, toggle }`. `createToolButton(type, behavior?)` (lines 232-285) builds the button: tooltip is `${label} — ${shortcut}` (line 254), shortcut badge via `keyBindingLabel` prop (lines 255-259) rendered by `IconButton` (`packages/excalidraw/components/IconButton.tsx:141-143/186-188`). Exported buttons like `LineToolButton = createToolButton("line")` (line 293) — a `"path"` tool would add a `TOOLS.path` entry plus `createToolButton("path")`.

**5. Group vs. single element vs. multi-ungrouped selection** — `appState.selectedElementIds` always holds individual element ids (map of `id -> true`); `appState.selectedGroupIds` (map of `groupId -> true`) is set separately when a whole group is selected (`selectGroup`, `packages/element/src/groups.ts`). Use `getSelectedGroupIds(appState)` (`groups.ts:234-239`, filters truthy entries) to detect:

- Exactly one group selected: `getSelectedGroupIds(appState).length === 1` (mirrors `actionGroup.tsx:108`).
- Exactly one ungrouped element: `getSelectedGroupIds(appState).length === 0 && Object.keys(appState.selectedElementIds).length === 1` (pattern from `actionFinalize.tsx:212`).
- Multiple ungrouped elements: `selectedElements.length >= 2 && !allElementsInSameGroup(selectedElements)` (`actionGroup.tsx:52-67, 80-83`). `getTargetElements`/`getSelectedElements` (`packages/element/src/selection.ts`) flatten a group selection into its constituent elements — `selectedElementIds` will contain every member id even when a single group is clicked, so group-vs-element discrimination must go through `selectedGroupIds`, not element count alone.

Since this issue's Head Issue (#18, motion) is clearly where real playback belongs, how should I handle this contradiction?**

Options:

- **Data/editing only, no playback (Recommended)** - Build path creation, multi-point editing, and element/group association only. 'Follow Path' is satisfied by the data model being playback-ready; actual animation is left entirely to issue #18.
- **Minimal non-persistent preview** - Add a bare-bones 'press and hold to preview' that slides the element along the path at a fixed speed with no easing/timing controls, just to visibly satisfy the 'Follow Path' criterion, still leaving the real motion system to #18.

**How should a motion path be represented in the element data model?**

Options:

- **New first-class element type 'path' (Recommended)** - Mirrors how 'frame'/'embeddable' were added: new entry in the ExcalidrawElement union, typeChecks.ts, restore.ts, renderElement.ts, newElement.ts. More files touched, but type-safe and consistent with codebase conventions, and sets up #18 cleanly.
- **Reuse 'line' element + customData flag** - Create it as an ordinary line element with customData.motionPath = { targetElementId } to mark it as a path. Much smaller diff (reuses all line rendering/editing/restore code as-is) but less type-safe and sends a mixed signal (it's selectable/editable as a generic line).

**How should a path be associated with 'a selected element or group', and can that association be changed later?**

Options:

- **Fixed at creation, element or native group (Recommended)** - Path stores targetElementId OR targetGroupId (Excalidraw's existing groupId), set when the path is drawn (user clicks the target first, like the issue's user scenario). Not re-targetable after creation — delete and redraw to change it.
- **Re-targetable after creation** - Same storage model, but add a UI affordance (e.g. in the properties panel) to re-pick the target element/group for an existing path after it's been drawn, adding more surface area now for a 'medium' scoped issue.

We're designing a new "Motion Path" feature for Excalidraw (issue #45, head issue #18 "Allow elements to have motion"). I need a detailed implementation plan for the DATA MODEL, TOOL, CREATION FLOW, and EDITING of the path element. A separate plan is being designed in parallel for the playback/animation mechanism (long-press-to-play) — do not design that; just define the minimal hook/interface the playback system will need (e.g. where path-to-target association and point data live, so animation code can read them).

## Confirmed design decisions (already made with the user, do not re-litigate):

1. The path is a new first-class element type `"path"` in the `ExcalidrawElement` union — NOT a customData flag on a line element. It should closely mirror `ExcalidrawLinearElement` (`type: "line" | "arrow"`, `points: readonly LocalPoint[]`) and reuse as much of the existing linear-element drawing/editing machinery as is practical (multi-point click-to-add-point drawing, `LinearElementEditor`-style post-creation point editing, `actionFinalize`-style Enter/Escape/double-click confirm).
2. Association to a target is fixed at creation time, stored as `targetElementId: string | null` OR `targetGroupId: GroupId | null` (mutually exclusive) — not re-targetable after creation.
3. User flow per the issue: user activates the "Path" tool from the toolbar → clicks the target element (or an element that's part of a group) on canvas to establish what the path will animate → then clicks to place path points (start, optional midpoints, end) like drawing a line → confirms (Enter/double-click/a "Done" button) to finalize the path.
4. Multiple independent paths can exist at once, each targeting a different element/group.
5. Out of scope for your plan: the actual animation/playback execution (frame-by-frame movement, speed, press-and-hold trigger) — another plan covers that. You only need to make sure the path element stores what playback will need: its ordered points and its target.

## Codebase facts gathered from exploration (verified by reading the files):

### Element type system

- `packages/element/src/types.ts`: `_ExcalidrawElementBase` (lines 40-82) has the common fields every element has: `id, x, y, strokeColor, backgroundColor, fillStyle, strokeWidth, strokeStyle, roundness, roughness, opacity, width, height, angle, seed, version, versionNonce, index, isDeleted, groupIds, frameId, boundElements, updated, link, locked, customData?`.
- `ExcalidrawLinearElement` (lines 340-348):

```ts
export type ExcalidrawLinearElement = _ExcalidrawElementBase &
  Readonly<{
    type: "line" | "arrow";
    points: readonly LocalPoint[];
    startBinding: FixedPointBinding | null;
    endBinding: FixedPointBinding | null;
    startArrowhead: Arrowhead | null;
    endArrowhead: Arrowhead | null;
  }>;
export type ExcalidrawLineElement = ExcalidrawLinearElement &
  Readonly<{
    type: "line";
    polygon: boolean;
  }>;
```

- `ExcalidrawElement` union (lines 211-221) currently: `ExcalidrawGenericElement | ExcalidrawTextElement | ExcalidrawLinearElement | ExcalidrawArrowElement | ExcalidrawFreeDrawElement | ExcalidrawImageElement | ExcalidrawFrameElement | ExcalidrawMagicFrameElement | ExcalidrawIframeElement | ExcalidrawEmbeddableElement`.
- `GroupId = string` (types.ts:24). `BoundElement = { id, type: "arrow" | "text" }` (types.ts:35-38) — the reverse-pointer pattern used for text-in-container and arrow bindings.
- Exhaustive type-guard switch: `isExcalidrawElement` in `packages/element/src/typeChecks.ts:246-275`, a `switch(type)` ending `default: assertNever(type, null)` — adding a new type requires a new `case` here or TypeScript's exhaustiveness check fails. Also note `isLinearElementType` (typeChecks.ts:152-158, currently `arrow"||"line"`), `isLineElement`/`isArrowElement`/`isLinearElement` (111-121, 105-109) as the guard patterns to mimic for e.g. `isPathElement`.
- `ExcalidrawBindableElement` union (types.ts:264-274) — things an arrow/binding can attach to (rectangle, diamond, triangle, ellipse, text, image, iframe, embeddable, frame, magicframe). Binding (`packages/element/src/binding.ts`) is element-to-element only via `FixedPointBinding { elementId, fixedPoint, mode }` — there is NO native "bind to a group" concept; group membership is just `element.groupIds: readonly GroupId[]`, resolved via `selectGroup` (`packages/element/src/groups.ts:24-60`) which scans elements for `groupIds.includes(groupId)`. So `targetGroupId` on the path element should just be a plain `GroupId` scanned against at use-time (this mirrors the existing `frameId` pattern: `_ExcalidrawElementBase.frameId: string | null`, resolved by scanning all elements for matching `frameId`, no reverse array needed) — simpler than the `containerId`/`boundElements` reverse-pointer pattern used for bound text, and you should prefer it for the same reason frames do: one-to-many, scan-based, no need to keep a reverse list in sync.

We're designing a new "Motion Path" feature for Excalidraw (issue #45, head issue #18 "Allow elements to have motion"). I need a detailed implementation plan for the PLAYBACK/ANIMATION mechanism only. ## Confirmed design decisions (already made with the user, do not re-litigate):

1. There is a new first-class element type `"path"` (like `ExcalidrawLinearElement` but its own type) with `points: readonly LocalPoint[]` (ordered, absolute-ish canvas coordinates the same way line/arrow points work — local to the path element's `x,y` origin) and a fixed-at-creation association to a target, stored as exactly one of `targetElementId: string | null` or `targetGroupId: GroupId | null` (GroupId = string).
2. User interaction trigger (confirmed by the user): **press and hold the target element for about a second, then the animation plays** — the element visually moves along its assigned path's points, in order, start to end.
3. Explicitly confirmed in scope for THIS issue: **a basic animation at a fixed, consistent base speed** (e.g. constant px/sec or constant total duration — your call, make a recommendation) with **no easing, no per-path speed/timing configuration, no scrubbing/playback controls**. This is deliberately simple — just "it moves along the path when triggered."
4. Explicitly out of scope (deferred to head issue #18): configurable speed/timing/easing curves, persisted animation/playback state, scrubbing or transport controls (play/pause/seek UI).
5. Multiple independent paths must be able to animate concurrently (e.g. two different elements each mid-animation along their own paths at the same time) — acceptance criterion "Multiple Path" from the issue.
6. Not required: motion data surviving save/reopen in a special persisted-animation-state sense (plain element data obviously persists normally since it's a regular element in the scene; it's specifically _animation playback state_ — e.g. "currently playing, at 40% progress" — that need not survive a reload).

## Codebase facts gathered from exploration (verified):

### Interaction/gesture precedent

- Excalidraw's pointer handling lives in `packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx`, which already has full pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup lifecycle handling and dispatches per-tool behavior based on `appState.activeTool.type` (the dispatch branch is around lines 8356-8397). Standard tool is `"selection"` — when the user is in selection mode and presses down on an element, that's the natural place to start a "press-and-hold" timer for this feature (so it doesn't require a dedicated tool to be active — the issue's user scenario says "Click and hold element for a second" while presumably in normal selection mode, after a path has already been created and confirmed for that element).
- There is no existing "long press" gesture helper in the codebase that we found in this exploration pass — you should design one (e.g. a `setTimeout`/`window.setTimeout` armed on pointerdown over a path-having element, cleared on pointerup/pointermove-past-threshold/pointerleave, matching the ~1 second mentioned in the issue's user scenario). Flag if you find an existing debounce/long-press utility worth reusing (e.g. search `packages/excalidraw/hooks` or `packages/common`) — if none exists, design a minimal one scoped to this feature rather than a generic reusable hook, per the project's "don't add abstractions beyond what's needed" convention.
- Excalidraw already runs a continuous animation/render loop pattern elsewhere for similar "animate a value over time and re-render" needs — e.g. check `packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx` and `packages/excalidraw/renderer/` for any existing `requestAnimationFrame` usage (e.g. laser pointer trails, eraser trail fade, or canvas animation helpers) and reuse that pattern/helper if one exists rather than inventing a second RAF loop mechanism. Search for `requestAnimationFrame` usage in `packages/excalidraw` before designing your own loop.

### Element update mechanism (how to actually move something each frame)

- Elements are mutated via `scene.mutateElement(element, { ...partialUpdate })` (seen in `packages/excalidraw/actions/actionFinalize.tsx` repeatedly, e.g. `scene.mutateElement(element, { points: ... })`) — this is the scene's element-mutation entrypoint; per-frame animation would call this (or a lower-overhead variant if `mutateElement` triggers expensive side effects like history capture on every call — investigate whether there's a way to mutate without pushing every frame onto undo/redo history, since animating 60 times/sec must NOT flood undo/redo. - Design the playback state as something that can track **multiple simultaneous animations** (one per path, each potentially targeting a different element/group), e.g. a small animation-state map keyed by path id or target id, each entry tracking `{ startTime, path, targetElementIds }`, driven by a single shared RAF loop that on each frame iterates all active animations and computes each one's current position via linear interpolation along the path's point sequence based on elapsed time vs. total duration (or vs. constant speed — your call per decision #3 above). 1	import { isRenderThrottlingEnabled } from "../reactUtils";
2
3	export type Animation<R extends object> = (params: {
4	  deltaTime: number;
5	  state?: R;
6	}) => R | null | undefined;
7
8	export class AnimationController {
9	  private static scheduledFrame:
10	    | { id: ReturnType<typeof requestAnimationFrame>; type: "raf" }
11	    | { id: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>; type: "timeout" }
12	    | null = null;
13	  private static animations = new Map<
14	    string,
15	    {
16	      animation: Animation<any>;
17	      lastTime: number;
18	      state: any;
19	    }
20	  >();
21
22	  static start<R extends object>(key: string, animation: Animation<R>) {
23	    if (AnimationController.animations.has(key)) {
24	      return;
25	    }
26
27	    const initialState = animation({
28	      deltaTime: 0,
29	      state: undefined,
30	    });
31
32	    if (initialState) {
33	      AnimationController.animations.set(key, {
34	        animation,
35	        lastTime: 0,
36	        state: initialState,
37	      });
38
39	      AnimationController.scheduleNextFrame();
40	    }
41	  }
42
43	  private static scheduleNextFrame() {
44	    if (AnimationController.scheduledFrame) {
45	      return;
46	    }
47
48	    if (isRenderThrottlingEnabled()) {
49	      AnimationController.scheduledFrame = {
50	        id: requestAnimationFrame(AnimationController.tick),
51	        type: "raf",
52	      };
53	    } else {
54	      AnimationController.scheduledFrame = {
55	        id: setTimeout(AnimationController.tick, 0),
56	        type: "timeout",
57	      };
58	    }
59	  }
60
61	  private static cancelScheduledFrame() {
62	    if (!AnimationController.scheduledFrame) {
63	      return;
64	    }
65
66	    if (AnimationController.scheduledFrame.type === "raf") {
67	      cancelAnimationFrame(AnimationController.scheduledFrame.id);
68	    } else {
69	      clearTimeout(AnimationController.scheduledFrame.id);
70	    }
71
72	    AnimationController.scheduledFrame = null;
73	  }
74
75	  private static cancelScheduledFrameIfIdle() {
76	    if (AnimationController.animations.size > 0) {
77	      return false;
78	    }
79
80	    AnimationController.cancelScheduledFrame();
81	    return true;
82	  }
83
84	  private static tick() {
85	    AnimationController.scheduledFrame = null;
86
87	    if (AnimationController.animations.size > 0) {
88	      for (const [key, animation] of AnimationController.animations) {
89	        const now = performance.now();
90	        const deltaTime =
91	          animation.lastTime === 0 ? 0 : now - animation.lastTime;
92
93	        const state = animation.animation({
94	          deltaTime,
95	          state: animation.state,
96	        });
97
98	        if (!state) {
99	          AnimationController.animations.delete(key);
100
101	          if (AnimationController.cancelScheduledFrameIfIdle()) {
102	            return;
103	          }
104	        } else {
105	          animation.lastTime = now;
106	          animation.state = state;
107	        }
108	      }
109
110	      if (AnimationController.cancelScheduledFrameIfIdle()) {
111	        return;
112	      }
113
114	      AnimationController.scheduleNextFrame();
115	    }
116	  }
117
118	  static running(key: string) {
119	    return AnimationController.animations.has(key);
120	  }
121
122	  static cancel(key: string) {
123	    AnimationController.animations.delete(key);
124	    AnimationController.cancelScheduledFrameIfIdle();
125	  }
126
127	  static reset() {
128	    AnimationController.animations.clear();
129	    AnimationController.cancelScheduledFrame();
130	  }
131	}

# Motion Path Feature — Implementation Plan (Data Model, Tool, Creation, Editing)

## 1. `ExcalidrawPathElement` type definition

**File: `packages/element/src/types.ts`**

Do **not** fold `path` into the `ExcalidrawLinearElement` union (I checked — see §5 below for why). Keep it a sibling type built directly on `_ExcalidrawElementBase`, structurally parallel to `ExcalidrawLinearElement` but without bindings/arrowheads, plus the two target fields:

```ts
export type ExcalidrawPathElement = _ExcalidrawElementBase &
  Readonly<{
    type: "path";
    points: readonly LocalPoint[];
    /** mutually exclusive with targetGroupId; resolved once at creation time */
    targetElementId: string | null;
    targetGroupId: GroupId | null;
  }>;
```

Add it to the union (types.ts:211-221):

```ts
export type ExcalidrawElement =
  | ExcalidrawGenericElement
  | ExcalidrawTextElement
  | ExcalidrawLinearElement
  | ExcalidrawArrowElement
  | ExcalidrawFreeDrawElement
  | ExcalidrawImageElement
  | ExcalidrawFrameElement
  | ExcalidrawMagicFrameElement
  | ExcalidrawIframeElement
  | ExcalidrawEmbeddableElement
  | ExcalidrawPathElement;
```

Invariant to document in a comment on the type: exactly one of `targetElementId`/`targetGroupId` is non-null (enforced at construction, never both). Consider a type-level encoding later (a discriminated union of the two cases) but a plain nullable pair mirrors the existing `startBinding`/`endBinding` style and is fine for v1 — flag this as a nice-to-have, not blocking.

### Type-system touchpoints (exhaustiveness)

- **`packages/element/src/typeChecks.ts:246-275`** — `isExcalidrawElement`'s switch needs `case "path": return true;` before `default: assertNever(...)`. This one is load-bearing: TS will fail to compile without it.
- Add guards mirroring `isLineElement`/`isArrowElement` (typeChecks.ts:111-121):

```ts
export const isPathElement = <T extends ExcalidrawElement>(
  element?: T | null,
): element is T & ExcalidrawPathElement => {
  return element != null && element.type === "path";
};
```

- **Do not** add `path` to `isLinearElementType` (typeChecks.ts:152-158) or `isBindingElementType` — paths are not bindable and should not be treated as linear elements by the ~50+ call sites that branch on `isLinearElement` for binding/arrowhead/resize behavior (properties panel arrowhead pickers, `maybeBindLinearElement`, elbow-arrow routing, etc.). Keeping path structurally separate avoids having to audit every one of those call sites for path-safety.
- **`packages/excalidraw/types.ts:145-162`** (`ToolType`) — add `"path"` to the union; `ElementOrToolType` (line 164) picks it up automatically since it derives from `ExcalidrawElementType | ToolType | "custom"`.
- Search for any other exhaustive switches over element type that will now fail to compile — run `tsc` after adding the union member and fix every "not assignable"/"missing case" error it surfaces (expect hits in `renderElement.ts`, `restore.ts`, `bounds.ts`, `staticSvgScene.ts`, possibly `packages/excalidraw/data/transform.ts` and the `@excalidraw/mermaid-to-excalidraw`/clipboard code — the compiler is the authoritative checklist here, don't hand-enumerate).

## 2. `newPathElement` constructor

**File: `packages/element/src/newElement.ts`**, placed next to `newLinearElement` (line 467):

```ts
export const newPathElement = (
  opts: {
    points?: ExcalidrawPathElement["points"];
    targetElementId?: string | null;
    targetGroupId?: GroupId | null;
  } & ElementConstructorOpts,
): NonDeleted<ExcalidrawPathElement> => {
  return {
    ..._newElementBase<ExcalidrawPathElement>("path", opts),
    points: opts.points || [],
    targetElementId: opts.targetElementId ?? null,
    targetGroupId: opts.targetGroupId ?? null,
  };
};
```

Caller is responsible for passing exactly one of `targetElementId`/`targetGroupId` (invariant-checked at the call site in App.tsx, not here — keep the constructor permissive/pure like its siblings).

## 3. Toolbar entry + pointer-down dispatch

### Toolbar

**`packages/excalidraw/components/Tools.tsx`**:

- Add an icon (new file entry in `packages/excalidraw/components/icons.tsx`, e.g. `PathIcon` — a dashed line with dot waypoints, distinct from `LineIcon`).
- Add to `TOOLS` (Tools.tsx:63-145):

```ts
path: {
  icon: PathIcon,
  letterKey: KEYS.M, // "M"otion path — L/A/etc already taken; pick an unused key
  fillable: false,
},
```

- Export `export const PathToolButton = createToolButton("path");` near line 293.

### Placement

Recommend the **`ExtraToolsDropdown`** in `packages/excalidraw/components/Toolbar.tsx:49-164` alongside `frame`/`embeddable`/`laser`/`lasso`, not the main row. Rationale: this is a power-user feature tied to a still-in-design playback system, the main toolbar is already dense, and other "sets up auxiliary structure on canvas" tools (frame) already live in the dropdown. Trade-off: lower discoverability — note this for the user to confirm, since it's a product call, not purely technical.

### Pointer-down dispatch

**`packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx`**, add a branch alongside the existing chain at lines 8356-8397:

```ts
} else if (this.state.activeTool.type === "path") {
  this.handlePathElementOnPointerDown(event, pointerDownState);
}
```

placed before the generic `createGenericElementOnPointerDown` fallback (it must not fall into that branch).

New private method `handlePathElementOnPointerDown`, modeled on `handleLinearElementOnPointerDown` (App.tsx:9511+), but with the two-phase behavior the user flow requires:

1. **No `appState.pendingPathTarget` yet (first click of this path)**: hit-test at the pointer position against `this.scene.getNonDeletedElements()` (reuse the existing element-under-cursor resolution already used for click-to-select, e.g. whatever `this.getElementAtPosition`/`hitTest` App.tsx uses for selection clicks — do not reimplement hit-testing).
   - **Hit** → resolve target (§7) and stash it in transient (non-undoable) state, e.g. `appState.pendingPathTarget: { elementId } | { groupId }`, set a transient cursor/indicator, and **do not** create any element yet or consume the click as a point.
   - **Miss** → no-op this click (stay in the "pick a target" sub-mode). Recommend also flashing a brief toast/hint ("Click an element to attach the path to") rather than silently doing nothing, for discoverability — flag as a UX nice-to-have, not core to this plan.
   - **Hit is itself a `path` element** → treat as a miss (paths are not valid targets — animating a path's motion along another path is out of scope and would create ambiguity in playback). Explicitly filter `isPathElement(hitElement)` out of the hit-test candidates for this first click.
2. **`appState.pendingPathTarget` already set (second and subsequent clicks)**: behaves like `handleLinearElementOnPointerDown`'s point-placement — first of these clicks calls `newPathElement({ points: [[0,0]], targetElementId / targetGroupId, x, y, ...baseProps })` and sets `appState.multiElement` + `appState.newElement` (same state shape as line/arrow multi-point drawing); subsequent clicks append points to `multiElement.points` exactly like `handleLinearElementOnPointerDown` does, including the `LINE_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD`/distance-to-last-point logic for "click near last point to finish" (reuse, don't duplicate — extract the shared point-append logic into a helper that both the line/arrow and path flows call if it isn't already factored out; check `handleLinearElementOnPointerDown`'s body for how cleanly this separates before committing to extraction vs. duplication — if it's heavily commingled with binding-suggestion logic, duplicating a slimmed-down ~20-line path-specific version is preferable to threading `isBindingElement` guards through the shared code for a feature that never binds).
   - **Do not** run `isPathALoop`/loop-closing logic for paths (next section) — a motion path closing into a loop has no special meaning here, unlike `line`.
   - **Do not** attempt start/end binding suggestion (`bindOrUnbindBindingElement`) — paths never bind their points to shapes.

Clear `appState.pendingPathTarget` whenever the path is finalized (§4) or the user cancels (Escape before any point is placed) or switches tools.

Add `pendingPathTarget` to `AppState`/`InteractiveCanvasAppState` in `packages/excalidraw/types.ts`, and make sure it's excluded from undo/redo history (it's transient UI state, not scene data) the same way `selectedLinearElement`/`multiElement` are handled by the store's `CaptureUpdateAction` classification — verify this in `packages/element/src/store.ts` (wherever `AppState` keys are classified into history-tracked vs not) and add it to the "ignore" list alongside similar transient fields.

## 4. Multi-point drawing/finalize flow

### Reused verbatim

- Point-append-on-click mechanics, `LINE_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD` distance check, `appState.multiElement`/`appState.newElement` state shape, pointer-move-while-drawing preview (`LinearElementEditor.handlePointerMove` equivalent — confirm it only touches `points`, not bindings, before reusing directly vs. writing a slim path-specific version per the typing discussion in §5).
- The "Done" button pattern and Enter/Escape finalize keybinding in `actionFinalize.tsx`.

### `actionFinalize.tsx` changes

**File: `packages/excalidraw/actions/actionFinalize.tsx`**

- `keyTest` (line 397-400) already fires on Escape/Enter whenever `appState.multiElement !== null` — no change needed, this is type-agnostic.
- `perform()`'s type-specific branches need a `path` no-op path through the special cases that currently assume line/arrow/freedraw:
  - Lines 207-219 (`element` resolution): `appState.newElement?.type === "freedraw" || isBindingElement(appState.newElement)` — for path, `appState.multiElement` already captures it at line 205-206 (`if (appState.multiElement) { element = appState.multiElement; }`), so no change needed there; a path mid-drawing is always in `multiElement`, never reaches the `isBindingElement` branch.
  - Lines 286-317 (loop-closing + polygon validity): guarded by `isLinearElement(element) || isFreeDrawElement(element)` and then narrowed further by `isLineElement`. Since `isPathElement` is deliberately **not** `isLinearElement`, this whole block is already skipped for path — **no code change required here**, which is a good sign the type separation (§1/§5) pays off by making this file mostly untouched.
  - Lines 342-345 (`selectedLinearElement = ... new LinearElementEditor(element, ...)`): currently gated on `isLinearElement(element)`. Decide: should finishing a path selection enter `LinearElementEditor`-style point-editing immediately (like line/arrow does)? Per the confirmed design (post-creation point editing should be supported), yes — so widen this condition to `isLinearElement(element) || isPathElement(element)` and make sure `LinearElementEditor`'s constructor and the handful of methods it's typed against accept `ExcalidrawPathElement` (see §5's resolution).
  - Point-count validation (`element.points.length < 2` discard, line 167 in the early-return branch, and implicitly elsewhere) applies uniformly and needs no path-specific change — a 1-point path is as invalid as a 1-point line.
- Net effect: `actionFinalize.tsx` needs exactly **one** line changed (the `selectedLinearElement` gate) plus the `isLinearElement` import list getting `isPathElement` added — contingent on the §5 decision being "yes, reuse `LinearElementEditor` for paths."

## 5. Post-creation point editing — `LinearElementEditor` reuse decision

I read `packages/element/src/linearElementEditor.ts` directly. Its ~30 method/static signatures are typed concretely as `ExcalidrawLinearElement` / `NonDeleted<ExcalidrawLinearElement>`, and a contiguous cluster of methods (around lines 2200-2470, plus the `createPointAt`/binding-suggestion logic in `handlePointerUp`) reads `.startBinding`/`.endBinding` **unconditionally** (not behind a type guard — just `if (element.startBinding)` on a param already typed as having that field). A blanket widen of every signature to a `ExcalidrawLinearElement | ExcalidrawPathElement` union would break compilation at every one of those reads, since `ExcalidrawPathElement` has no such field.

**Recommendation — surgical widen, not blanket widen:**

1. Introduce a local union alias in `linearElementEditor.ts` (or `types.ts`) scoped to editing geometry only:

     | ExcalidrawLinearElement
     | ExcalidrawPathElement;

2. Widen **only** the entry points actually invoked from pointer interaction and point-geometry mutation, i.e. (confirm exact set while implementing, but based on what I read): `getElement`, `handlePointerDown`, `handlePointerMove`, `handlePointerMoveInEditMode`, `handlePointerUp` (the point-dragging path, not the binding-suggestion branch inside it — that branch is already gated by `isBindingElement(element)` which is `false` for path, so it's dead code for paths even if the surrounding function signature is widened), `getPointIndexUnderCursor`, `addMidpoint`, `movePoints` (the pure point-position-update overload), `getNormalizeElementPointsAndCoords`.

This is mechanical but non-trivial — treat it as its own implementation sub-task with its own test pass (`packages/element/tests/linearElementEditor.test.tsx` likely needs new path-specific cases), not a drive-by change. ## 7. `targetElementId` / `targetGroupId` resolution at creation time

**Recommendation**, validated against `groups.ts`/`selection.ts`:

On the first click of the path tool (§3, step 1), given the hit element `el`:

```ts
if (el.groupIds.length > 0) {
  // shallowest (outermost) group — groupIds is ordered deepest-to-shallowest
  // per the documented invariant in types.ts:71-72, so the outermost is the LAST entry
  targetGroupId = el.groupIds[el.groupIds.length - 1];
  targetElementId = null;
} else {
  targetElementId = el.id;
  targetGroupId = null;
}
```

This matches the canonical "select the whole group when clicking a member" behavior elsewhere (`selectGroupsForSelectedElements` in `groups.ts` and the normal canvas click-to-select-group flow) which also resolves to the outermost group for a multi-grouped element. Double-check this against `selectGroupsForSelectedElements`'s actual outermost-group resolution logic while implementing (I confirmed `groupIds` ordering semantics from the type doc comment and `selectGroup`'s membership-scan, but did not trace the exact "which group wins when nested" call site end-to-end — do that as a one-line sanity check before writing this code, since getting deepest-vs-shallowest backwards here would silently mistarget nested groups).

Validate the resolved target is not a `path` element itself (§3) and not a `selection`-type pseudo-element (shouldn't be hit-testable anyway).

## 8. Interface for the (separately designed) playback system

Put this in a new small module, **`packages/element/src/path.ts`**, so both this feature and the playback feature import from one place rather than duplicating target-resolution logic:

```ts
// packages/element/src/path.ts
import { isPathElement } from "./typeChecks";
import type { ExcalidrawElement, ExcalidrawPathElement, ElementsMapOrArray, NonDeletedExcalidrawElement } from "./types";

/** Resolves a path's target to the concrete element(s) it should animate.
 *  Returns [] if the target no longer exists (deleted target, dangling id/groupId). */
export const getPathTargetElements = (
  path: ExcalidrawPathElement,
  elements: ElementsMapOrArray,
): NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[] => {
  if (path.targetElementId) {
    const el = /* lookup by id in elements */;
    return el && !el.isDeleted ? [el] : [];
  }
  if (path.targetGroupId) {
    return /* scan elements for groupIds.includes(path.targetGroupId) && !isDeleted */;
  }
  return [];
};

/** All paths in the scene that target a given element (directly or via its group). */
export const getPathsTargetingElement = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  elements: ElementsMapOrArray,
): ExcalidrawPathElement[] => { /* scan for isPathElement && (targetElementId === element.id || element.groupIds.includes(targetGroupId)) */ };
```

What playback needs to read, and where it lives:

- **Ordered points**: `pathElement.points: readonly LocalPoint[]` — local coordinates; playback will need `pathElement.x`/`pathElement.y` (the element's own origin, same convention as line/arrow) to get them into scene/global space — same transform `LinearElementEditor.getPointAtIndexGlobalCoordinates` already performs for line/arrow, reusable as-is since `path` has the same `x`/`y`/`points` shape.
- **Target resolution**: `getPathTargetElements(path, elements)` above — returns the live element(s) to move. For a group target this returns all current members (handles members added/removed from the group after path creation gracefully, since resolution is scan-based at read time, not baked in).
- **Association direction**: it's one-way (`path → target`), there is intentionally no reverse pointer on the target element (consistent with the `frameId` precedent cited in the facts). If playback needs "does this element have any animating path" it should call `getPathsTargetingElement`, not expect a field on the target.
- **Multiplicity**: playback must independently handle N paths each targeting possibly-overlapping or possibly-different elements (confirmed design point 4) — `getPathsTargetingElement` can return more than one.

### Edge cases to carry into both plans

- **Target element deleted while a path references it**: `getPathTargetElements` returns `[]`; the path element itself is untouched (not auto-deleted) — it becomes an inert/orphaned path. Recommend the selection/properties UI show a visual "broken" indicator (e.g. greyed stroke) when `getPathTargetElements(path, elements).length === 0`; this is a small addition to the render case in §6, worth including rather than deferring, since a silently-dead path with no visual cue is a bad UX trap.
- **Target group fully disbanded** (ungroup action removes `groupIds` from all members): same as above — `getPathTargetElements` naturally returns `[]` once no element's `groupIds` contains `targetGroupId` anymore; no special-case code needed given the scan-based design.
- **Deleting a path element**: fully standard element deletion — no cleanup needed elsewhere since nothing points back to it (confirms the frame-style one-way reference was the right call).
- **Undo/redo**: path creation/point-edits go through the normal `CaptureUpdateAction` mutation flow exactly like line/arrow (via `scene.mutateElement`/`newElementWith`), so standard undo/redo "just works" for the element data. The one new piece of transient, non-undoable state is `appState.pendingPathTarget` (§3) — must be excluded from history capture the same way `multiElement`/`selectedLinearElement` already are; verify in the store's history-key classification.
- **First click (target-pick phase) hits another path element**: treated as a miss (§3) — prevents chaining/targeting paths at other paths, which playback isn't designed to support.
- **First click hits a frame**: frames are in `ExcalidrawBindableElement` conceptually but not in the resolution logic above — recommend treating a frame hit the same as any other element (`targetElementId = frame.id`), since frames are valid, ordinary elements with their own `groupIds`/`id`; playback's definition of "move the target" for a frame (does it drag its children too?) is explicitly out of scope for this plan and should be a question for the playback design.

This also sidesteps `ShapeCache` invalidation semantics tied to `roughness`/`seed` that don't meaningfully apply to a path.
- **`renderElement.ts`**: three touchpoints:

Keep it simple (no roughjs) — direct canvas `moveTo`/`lineTo` + `arc()` for the dots, same technique already used for things like the "Done"/selection resize handles.

### Restore (`packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts`)

Add a `case "path":` in `restoreElement`'s per-type switch near line 577, modeled on the `"line"` case (restore.ts:577-620) but without the `startArrowhead`/`startBinding` normalization:

```ts
case "path": {
  const points = restoreLinearElementPoints(element.points, element.width, element.height);
  return restoreElementWithProperties(element, {
    points,
    targetElementId: element.targetElementId ?? null,
    targetGroupId: element.targetGroupId ?? null,
    ...getSizeFromPoints(points),
  });
}
```

Edge case to handle explicitly here or in a post-restore validation pass (see §8): if `targetElementId` references an element that no longer exists in the restored scene (e.g. partial/corrupt import, or cross-scene paste), **do not throw** — leave the dangling id; resolution of "does my target still exist" is a read-time concern for whoever consumes the path (selection UI, playback), not a restore-time concern, consistent with how `frameId` dangling references are already tolerated elsewhere in the codebase.

- **`packages/element/src/collision.ts`**: line 505-513, add `"path"` to the existing `case "line": case "freedraw": case "arrow":` group calling `intersectLinearOrFreeDrawWithLineSegment` — this is a direct drop-in since the function only needs `.points`.

- **`packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts`**: flag only — needs a matching dashed-stroke-plus-dots case so exported SVGs look the same. Not deeply designed here.

## 7. `targetElementId` / `targetGroupId` resolution at creation time

**Recommendation**, validated against `groups.ts`/`selection.ts`:

On the first click of the path tool (§3, step 1), given the hit element `el`:

```ts
if (el.groupIds.length &gt; 0) {
  // shallowest (outermost) group — groupIds is ordered deepest-to-shallowest
  // per the documented invariant in types.ts:71-72, so the outermost is the LAST entry
  targetGroupId = el.groupIds[el.groupIds.length - 1];
  targetElementId = null;
} else {
  targetElementId = el.id;
  targetGroupId = null;
}
```

This matches the canonical "select the whole group when clicking a member" behavior elsewhere (`selectGroupsForSelectedElements` in `groups.ts` and the normal canvas click-to-select-group flow) which also resolves to the outermost group for a multi-grouped element. Double-check this against `selectGroupsForSelectedElements`'s actual outermost-group resolution logic while implementing (I confirmed `groupIds` ordering semantics from the type doc comment and `selectGroup`'s membership-scan, but did not trace the exact "which group wins when nested" call site end-to-end — do that as a one-line sanity check before writing this code, since getting deepest-vs-shallowest backwards here would silently mistarget nested groups).

Validate the resolved target is not a `path` element itself (§3) and not a `selection`-type pseudo-element (shouldn't be hit-testable anyway).

## 8. Interface for the (separately designed) playback system

Put this in a new small module, **`packages/element/src/path.ts`**, so both this feature and the playback feature import from one place rather than duplicating target-resolution logic:

```ts
// packages/element/src/path.ts
import { isPathElement } from "./typeChecks";
import type { ExcalidrawElement, ExcalidrawPathElement, ElementsMapOrArray, NonDeletedExcalidrawElement } from "./types";

/** Resolves a path's target to the concrete element(s) it should animate.
 *  Returns [] if the target no longer exists (deleted target, dangling id/groupId). */
export const getPathTargetElements = (
  path: ExcalidrawPathElement,
  elements: ElementsMapOrArray,
): NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[] =&gt; {
  if (path.targetElementId) {
    const el = /* lookup by id in elements */;
    return el &amp;&amp; !el.isDeleted ? [el] : [];
  }
  if (path.targetGroupId) {
    return /* scan elements for groupIds.includes(path.targetGroupId) &amp;&amp; !isDeleted */;
  }
  return [];
};

/** All paths in the scene that target a given element (directly or via its group). */
export const getPathsTargetingElement = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  elements: ElementsMapOrArray,
): ExcalidrawPathElement[] =&gt; { /* scan for isPathElement &amp;&amp; (targetElementId === element.id || element.groupIds.includes(targetGroupId)) */ };
```

What playback needs to read, and where it lives:

- **Ordered points**: `pathElement.points: readonly LocalPoint[]` — local coordinates; playback will need `pathElement.x`/`pathElement.y` (the element's own origin, same convention as line/arrow) to get them into scene/global space — same transform `LinearElementEditor.getPointAtIndexGlobalCoordinates` already performs for line/arrow, reusable as-is since `path` has the same `x`/`y`/`points` shape.
- **Target resolution**: `getPathTargetElements(path, elements)` above — returns the live element(s) to move. For a group target this returns all current members (handles members added/removed from the group after path creation gracefully, since resolution is scan-based at read time, not baked in).
- **Association direction**: it's one-way (`path → target`), there is intentionally no reverse pointer on the target element (consistent with the `frameId` precedent cited in the facts). If playback needs "does this element have any animating path" it should call `getPathsTargetingElement`, not expect a field on the target.
- **Multiplicity**: playback must independently handle N paths each targeting possibly-overlapping or possibly-different elements (confirmed design point 4) — `getPathsTargetingElement` can return more than one.

### Edge cases to carry into both plans

- **Target element deleted while a path references it**: `getPathTargetElements` returns `[]`; the path element itself is untouched (not auto-deleted) — it becomes an inert/orphaned path. Recommend the selection/properties UI show a visual "broken" indicator (e.g. greyed stroke) when `getPathTargetElements(path, elements).length === 0`; this is a small addition to the render case in §6, worth including rather than deferring, since a silently-dead path with no visual cue is a bad UX trap.
- **Target group fully disbanded** (ungroup action removes `groupIds` from all members): same as above — `getPathTargetElements` naturally returns `[]` once no element's `groupIds` contains `targetGroupId` anymore; no special-case code needed given the scan-based design.
- **Deleting a path element**: fully standard element deletion — no cleanup needed elsewhere since nothing points back to it (confirms the frame-style one-way reference was the right call).
- **Undo/redo**: path creation/point-edits go through the normal `CaptureUpdateAction` mutation flow exactly like line/arrow (via `scene.mutateElement`/`newElementWith`), so standard undo/redo "just works" for the element data. The one new piece of transient, non-undoable state is `appState.pendingPathTarget` (§3) — must be excluded from history capture the same way `multiElement`/`selectedLinearElement` already are; verify in the store's history-key classification.
- **First click (target-pick phase) hits another path element**: treated as a miss (§3) — prevents chaining/targeting paths at other paths, which playback isn't designed to support.
- **First click hits a frame**: frames are in `ExcalidrawBindableElement` conceptually but not in the resolution logic above — recommend treating a frame hit the same as any other element (`targetElementId = frame.id`), since frames are valid, ordinary elements with their own `groupIds`/`id`; playback's definition of "move the target" for a frame (does it drag its children too?) is explicitly out of scope for this plan and should be a question for the playback design.

# Motion Path — Playback/Animation Mechanism: Implementation Plan

This plan covers only the trigger gesture, the animation driver, element mutation, and state lifecycle. It treats the `"path"` element type, `targetElementId`/`targetGroupId`, and `points: readonly LocalPoint[]` as a given interface from the parallel data-model plan.

## 0. Key discoveries that shape the design

- **A generic, keyed, shared animation driver already exists**: `packages/excalidraw/renderer/animation.ts` — `AnimationController`. It supports multiple concurrently-running, independently-keyed animations off a single RAF (or `setTimeout` fallback when render-throttling is disabled), each with its own per-tick `state` and `deltaTime`. It's already used for viewport fly-to animation (`packages/excalidraw/viewport.ts`, key `SCROLL_TO_CONTENT_ANIMATION_KEY`) and the laser/eraser trails (`packages/excalidraw/animatedTrail.ts`). **This is exactly the mechanism needed for concurrent path playback — do not build a second RAF loop.** Use `AnimationController.start(key, animation)` / `.cancel(key)` / `.running(key)`.
- **Ephemeral, non-persisted "runtime" state belongs on the `App` class instance, not in `appState`.** Precedent: `laserTrails = new LaserTrails(this)` and `eraserTrail = new EraserTrail(this)` at `packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx:755-756`, and `private bindModeHandler: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;` (~line 733) for an armed "hold" timer. Every `appState` key must additionally be registered in `APP_STATE_STORAGE_CONF` in `packages/excalidraw/appState.ts` (all `false` by default) for `clearAppStateForLocalStorage`/export/database filtering — adding a new appState key is strictly more ceremony than a class field for something that must never persist, never undo, and never diff against `ObservedAppState`. **Recommendation: a plain `App` class field**, not appState.
- **`CaptureUpdateAction` only controls undo/redo capture — it does not stop `onChange`.** `componentDidUpdate` (App.tsx ~3694-3703) calls `this.store.commit(...)` _and_ `this.props.onChange?.(...)` on every render, unconditionally. `CaptureUpdateAction` (`packages/element/src/store.ts`) governs only what `store.commit` does with the diff (`IMMEDIATELY` → pushed to undo stack now; `EVENTUALLY` → deferred/merged into the next `IMMEDIATELY`; `NEVER` → discarded, never recorded). The default when nothing is scheduled this tick is `EVENTUALLY` (`store.ts` `getScheduledMacroAction`).
- **The existing drag-to-move flow is the precedent for "many per-frame mutations → one undo entry."** During pointermove, `dragSelectedElements` (`packages/element/src/dragElements.ts`) calls `scene.mutateElement` repeatedly with no explicit capture scheduling (falls through to default `EVENTUALLY`); on pointerup, `this.store.scheduleCapture()` is called exactly once (e.g. `App.tsx:11001`, `:11246`, `:11490`) to collapse the whole gesture into a single `IMMEDIATELY` history entry. Other one-off "discard this mutation" sites explicitly call `this.store.scheduleAction(CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER)` (e.g. `App.tsx:12223`, `:8080`, `:3127`, `:11321`, `:11499`) — this is the idiom to copy for "this mutation must never be undoable."
- **Group → elements resolution already exists and is reused elsewhere**: `Scene.getElementsFromId(id)` (`packages/element/src/Scene.ts:397-407`) does precisely "if `id` is an element id, return `[element]`; otherwise treat it as a group id and call `getElementsInGroup(elementsMap, id)`" (`packages/element/src/groups.ts:289`). This is a direct match for resolving `targetElementId ?? targetGroupId` to a concrete element list — no new resolution logic needed.
- **Rigid-body group translation precedent**: `dragSelectedElements`/`updateElementCoords` in `packages/element/src/dragElements.ts:204-220` — captures each element's _original_ `x`/`y` (from `pointerDownState.originalElements`), then every tick sets `x = originalX + offset.x`, `y = originalY + offset.y` via `scene.mutateElement`. This is simpler than reusing the function wholesale (it's entangled with `PointerDownState`, snapping, elbow-arrow rebinding, frame membership) — the plan below extracts just the "capture original positions once, translate by a delta every tick" shape of it, not the function itself.
- **No existing long-press/hold helper.** The closest precedent is `bindModeHandler` (a raw `setTimeout` id stored as a nullable class field, armed/cleared directly in pointer handlers) — follow that pattern rather than introducing a generic hook.
- **No existing polyline length/arc-length utility** (expected, since the `path` element doesn't exist yet). A small new module is needed (detailed in §7).

## 1. Press-and-hold gesture detection

**Where it hooks in:** `packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx`, inside the existing pointerdown handler for the `"selection"` tool (the branch guarded by `this.state.activeTool.type === "selection"`, where `pointerDownState.hit.element` is already resolved — see assignments around `App.tsx:8895-8976`). This runs regardless of what else selection-mode pointerdown does (selecting/preparing to drag); it does not require a new tool.

**New `App` class fields** (next to `bindModeHandler`, ~line 733):

```ts
private pathPlaybackArmTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
private pathPlaybackArmedAt: { x: number; y: number } | null = null; // pointerdown coords, for move-threshold check
```

**Logic, added at the end of the existing pointerdown selection branch** (near `App.tsx:8356`, right after the current hit/selection bookkeeping, as a new private method `private armPathPlaybackIfApplicable(pointerDownState, hitElement)`):

1. Resolve whether `hitElement` has an associated path. This requires one new read-only lookup supplied by (or added alongside) the data-model plan: `scene.getPathForTarget(elementId)` or equivalent — scanning scene elements for a `"path"` element whose `targetElementId === hitElement.id` or whose `targetGroupId` is one of `hitElement.groupIds`. If none, do nothing (plain selection/drag proceeds untouched).
2. If found and no animation is already running for this path (see §6 "already mid-animation" below), arm: `this.pathPlaybackArmedAt = { x: pointerDownState.origin.x, y: pointerDownState.origin.y }` and `this.pathPlaybackArmTimer = setTimeout(() => this.startPathPlayback(path, hitElement), PATH_PLAYBACK_HOLD_MS)` where `PATH_PLAYBACK_HOLD_MS = 1000` is a new constant (co-located with `DRAGGING_THRESHOLD` in `packages/common/src/constants.ts`, or locally in App.tsx next to `BIND_MODE_TIMEOUT` if that constant's module is more appropriate — match whichever module `BIND_MODE_TIMEOUT` lives in).

**Cancellation (mirrors `bindModeHandler`'s clear sites and the `DRAGGING_THRESHOLD`-based cancel at `App.tsx:6980`):**

- **On pointermove**, in the existing generic pointermove handler (same place that computes `draggedDistance` / handles `DRAGGING_THRESHOLD`, ~`App.tsx:1444` pattern, or the per-gesture pointermove branch that follows pointerdown): if `this.pathPlaybackArmTimer` is set and the move distance from `pathPlaybackArmedAt` exceeds `DRAGGING_THRESHOLD` (same constant already imported, `packages/common/src/constants.ts:19`, value `10`px), call `clearTimeout(this.pathPlaybackArmTimer); this.pathPlaybackArmTimer = null;`. This is what lets a normal drag-to-move proceed unimpeded — if the user is actually dragging, the gesture naturally exceeds 10px well before 1000ms and the long-press is cancelled, so there is no conflict with drag-to-move.
- **On pointerup** (top of the existing `onPointerUp`/`handlePointerUp`, unconditionally, before any other branching): same clear. This is what lets a normal quick click/selection proceed unimpeded — if the user releases before 1000ms, the timer never fires, selection behaves exactly as today.
- **On pointer leaving the canvas / pointercancel**: same clear, added to the existing `pointerleave`/blur handlers used for other armed timers/drags.
- A long-press that _does_ fire (full 1000ms held without exceeding the move threshold) should **not** additionally trigger the normal click/select/drag outcome for that pointerdown — set a `pointerDownState.hit.wasPathPlaybackTriggered = true`-style flag (or simply check `this.pathPlaybackArmTimer === null && <animation started>` at the top of pointerup) so pointerup's normal "this was a click" logic short-circuits. Concretely: once `startPathPlayback` fires, null out `this.pathPlaybackArmTimer` and set a transient flag read once by the pointerup handler to skip the click-selection branch for that gesture (selection itself — the element becoming selected — can still be allowed to stand; only "click toggled selection a second time" / "treated as a completed short click" needs suppressing). This needs a small, explicit one-off boolean rather than reusing `pointerDownState.hit.wasAddedToSelection`, to avoid coupling to unrelated selection semantics.

**No new generic "long-press hook" abstraction** — per the project's existing convention (raw `setTimeout` id as a class field, `bindModeHandler`), this is implemented as two class fields and ~15 lines across pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup, not a reusable hook.

## 2. Resolving target(s) to move

New function, colocated with other path-specific geometry (either a new `packages/element/src/path.ts`, or appended to wherever the data-model plan already puts path-specific helpers — confirm file name with that plan):

```ts
// packages/element/src/path.ts
export const getPathTargetElements = (
  scene: Scene,
  path: ExcalidrawPathElement,
): NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[] => {
  const id = path.targetElementId ?? path.targetGroupId;
  if (!id) return [];
  return scene.getElementsFromId(id); // already handles "element id" vs "group id" uniformly
};
```

This is a thin wrapper — `Scene.getElementsFromId` (`packages/element/src/Scene.ts:397-407`) already does the element-vs-group disambiguation and calls `getElementsInGroup` (`packages/element/src/groups.ts:289`) for the group case. No new group-membership logic is written.

Also resolve and move each target's **bound text element**, mirroring `dragSelectedElements`'s handling (`getBoundTextElement(element, elementsMap)`, `packages/element/src/textElement.ts`) — if a target (or a group member) is a container with bound text, the text must translate with it or it will visually detach during playback.
