## 3. Animation loop design

**Driver:** `AnimationController` (`packages/excalidraw/renderer/animation.ts`) — one `AnimationController.start(key, animation)` call per triggered path, keyed by e.g. `` `path-playback-${path.id}` ``. Multiple concurrent triggers simply register multiple keys; `AnimationController` already multiplexes them over its single shared scheduled frame (`tick()` iterates `AnimationController.animations` each frame — `animation.ts:84-116`), satisfying the "Multiple Path" concurrency requirement with zero new scheduling code.

**New module**: `packages/excalidraw/pathPlayback.ts` (new file, App-adjacent like `animatedTrail.ts`), exporting a small `PathPlaybackController` class instantiated once on `App` (`pathPlayback = new PathPlaybackController(this)`, next to `laserTrails`/`eraserTrail` at `App.tsx:755-756`).

```ts
type PlaybackState = {
  elapsed: number; // ms
  totalDuration: number; // ms, computed once at start
  pathId: string;
  originalPositions: Map<string, { x: number; y: number }>; // targetId -> original x/y
  pathPoints: readonly LocalPoint[];
};

class PathPlaybackController {
  constructor(private app: App) {}

  start(path: ExcalidrawPathElement, targets: NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[]) {
    const key = `path-playback-${path.id}`;
    if (AnimationController.running(key)) return; // see §6 "restart vs ignore"

    const length = getPathLength(path.points);
    const totalDuration = (length / PATH_PLAYBACK_SPEED_PX_PER_SEC) * 1000;
    const originalPositions = new Map(
      targets.map((el) => [el.id, { x: el.x, y: el.y }]),
    );

    AnimationController.start<PlaybackState>(key, ({ deltaTime, state }) => {
      const next: PlaybackState = state
        ? { ...state, elapsed: state.elapsed + deltaTime }
        : {
            elapsed: 0,
            totalDuration,
            pathId: path.id,
            originalPositions,
            pathPoints: path.points,
          };

      const t = Math.min(next.elapsed / next.totalDuration, 1);
      const { x: dx, y: dy } = getPointAtProgress(next.pathPoints, t);
      const { x: startDx, y: startDy } = next.pathPoints[0];

      for (const target of targets) {
        const orig = next.originalPositions.get(target.id)!;
        this.app.scene.mutateElement(
          target,
          { x: orig.x + (dx - startDx), y: orig.y + (dy - startDy) },
          { informMutation: true, isDragging: true },
        );
      }
      this.app.store.scheduleAction(CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER); // never undoable per-frame

      if (t >= 1) {
        this.finish(path.id, targets, next.originalPositions);
        return null; // AnimationController deregisters the key
      }
      return next;
    });
  }

  private finish(pathId, targets, originalPositions) {
    // see §5 for end-of-animation behavior
  }

  cancel(pathId: string) {
    AnimationController.cancel(`path-playback-${pathId}`);
  }
}
```

Notes on this design:

- **Constant speed, not fixed duration** — `PATH_PLAYBACK_SPEED_PX_PER_SEC` (new constant, recommend **300px/sec** as a starting default, tunable without redesign) is computed against the path's total length (`getPathLength`, §7) once at start, giving `totalDuration`. This satisfies "fixed, consistent base speed" (decision #3) while naturally giving longer paths longer playback — more intuitive than a fixed duration where a long path would suddenly move very fast relative to a short one. (A fixed-duration alternative is one constant away — `totalDuration = 1000` instead of length/speed — if the user prefers that; flagging as a one-line decision, not an architecture fork.)
- **Linear interpolation along the ordered point sequence, not just a straight line from start to end** — `getPointAtProgress` (§7) must walk the segments by cumulative length so the element visibly follows every vertex of the path, not just interpolate between the first and last point.
- **Per-frame capture is explicitly `NEVER`, every tick**, not left to default `EVENTUALLY`. This is deliberately stronger than the drag precedent: with drag, nothing else is likely to schedule `IMMEDIATELY` mid-gesture, so relying on default `EVENTUALLY` + a single terminal `scheduleCapture()` is safe. With animation, the gesture can run for a few seconds, during which _unrelated_ user actions (e.g., editing a different element) could call `scheduleCapture()` first — since `getScheduledMacroAction` gives `IMMEDIATELY` precedence over any pending `EVENTUALLY`, that would sweep the moving element's current mid-flight frame into the user's unrelated undo entry. Explicitly scheduling `NEVER` every tick avoids that entirely (consistent with how `NEVER` is used elsewhere for "this specific mutation must never be recorded," e.g. `App.tsx:12223`, `:8080`).
- **`isDragging: true`** passed to `mutateElement`'s options mirrors how drag/bind-mode-style continuous repositioning already flags itself (see `App.tsx:1280-1292` and `dragElements.ts`), rather than inventing a new option value.
- **One shared RAF per frame drives all concurrent playbacks**, and because React 18 batches `setState` calls issued synchronously within one callback, multiple targets' `mutateElement` calls inside the same `AnimationController.tick()` invocation collapse into a single re-render (`Scene.triggerUpdate` → `App.triggerRender` → `this.setState({})`) regardless of how many paths are animating that frame.

**Known residual concern — collab/localStorage write frequency**: `componentDidUpdate` calls `this.props.onChange` on every re-render **regardless of `CaptureUpdateAction`** (`App.tsx:3694-3703`). In `excalidraw-app/App.tsx:679-734`, `onChange` synchronously calls `collabAPI.syncElements(elements)` → `Collab.tsx:954` `broadcastElements` with no throttle, and schedules a `LocalData.save`. A ~60fps (or even throttled ~24-30fps) playback will therefore still cause one `onChange`/broadcast per rendered frame while any path is playing. This is **not fixable from within `packages/excalidraw` alone** — it's a property of the host app's `onChange` handler. Two mitigations, neither required for this issue but worth flagging for the user:

1. Throttle the playback tick itself (e.g. target ~30fps instead of every RAF frame, using the `deltaTime` `AnimationController` already supplies — skip mutating until `elapsed since last mutate >= ~33ms`), halving the broadcast rate for a still-smooth basic animation.
2. A follow-up (likely head issue #18 territory, since it touches collab) to make `excalidraw-app/collab/Collab.tsx`'s `broadcastElements` throttle-coalesce bursts of same-tick element updates, independent of this feature. I recommend doing (1) now (cheap, local, no cross-cutting change) and explicitly deferring (2).

---

## 4. Where playback state lives

**Recommendation: `App` class instance fields**, not `appState`. Concretely:

- `pathPlayback: PathPlaybackController` — instance of the new controller above, holding nothing persisted; its only state is what's inside `AnimationController`'s private `animations` map (keyed by path id), which itself is a `static` module-level map, not tied to React state/appState at all.
- `pathPlaybackArmTimer` / `pathPlaybackArmedAt` (§1) — tiny gesture-arming state, same category as `bindModeHandler`.

Reasoning, directly from the codebase's own convention: `appState` keys are either persisted-by-default or must be explicitly whitelisted per export target in `APP_STATE_STORAGE_CONF` (`packages/excalidraw/appState.ts:~200-266`), and are part of `ObservedAppState`/history delta comparisons (`packages/element/src/delta.ts`, `AppStateDelta`) — i.e., putting playback progress in `appState` would make it a candidate for diffing/observation machinery designed for user-facing, undo-relevant state. The two existing "ephemeral per-frame visual state" features (laser trail, eraser trail) both avoid `appState` entirely and live as plain class fields (`App.tsx:755-756`) wrapping their own internal mutable state (`AnimatedTrail`'s `currentTrail`/`pastTrails`, in `packages/excalidraw/animatedTrail.ts`) — this feature matches that shape closely enough to copy it directly rather than inventing a third pattern.

---

## 5. End-of-animation behavior (needs user confirmation — flagging as an open decision)

Two reasonable options:

- **Option A — snap back to the pre-animation position (recommended).** `finish()` restores `target.x/y` to the captured `originalPositions` for every target, then calls `this.app.store.scheduleAction(CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER)` once more (net position change across the whole gesture is zero, so there is nothing meaningful to make undoable, and no stray entry risks confusing `Ctrl+Z`). This matches the "press-and-hold to **preview** motion" framing of the trigger gesture — it behaves like a repeatable preview/demo rather than a destructive edit, is safe to trigger accidentally or repeatedly, and keeps the element's canonical diagram position exactly as the user placed it regardless of how many times playback runs. It also sidesteps needing to decide what "redo the same animation after it ended at the destination" should even mean for a second trigger.
- **Option B — leave the element at the path's end.** `finish()` does nothing further (element stays wherever the last frame left it), and calls `this.app.store.scheduleCapture()` once (so the whole displacement from start → end collapses into exactly one `IMMEDIATELY` undo entry, same as a normal drag). This matches tools like PowerPoint's default motion-path behavior (object stays at the path's end after the effect plays) and may be what users expect if they're using the path to permanently reposition an element via "play."

**I recommend Option A** given the "press-and-hold to trigger, no scrubbing/transport controls" framing suggests a preview-style interaction rather than an editing action, and because it composes more simply with "trigger again" (§6) — but this is explicitly a product decision, not an architectural one, and should be confirmed with the user before implementation. The code difference between the two is isolated entirely to the ~6-line `finish()` method.

---

## 6. Edge cases

- **Re-triggering an already-animating target**: `PathPlaybackController.start()` checks `AnimationController.running(key)` and currently **ignores** the new trigger if already running (simplest, avoids visual popping from restarting mid-flight). An alternative ("restart from the top") is a one-line change — `AnimationController.cancel(key)` before `.start()` — flagging this as a minor, easy-to-swap decision alongside §5, not a structural one. Recommend **ignore** to start, since it's the conservative default and restart is strictly easier to add later than to remove the cancel-and-rerun semantics once users depend on it.
- **Target element deleted mid-animation**: each tick, before mutating, filter `targets` to currently-non-deleted elements (`!this.app.scene.getElement(id)?.isDeleted`); if the _entire_ target set becomes empty, return `null` from the `AnimationController` callback immediately (ending the animation early, no `finish()` repositioning needed since there's nothing left to reposition). This requires re-resolving via `scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap()` each tick rather than closing over a stale array, since the Scene mutates in place.
- **Path element deleted mid-animation**: the path's `points`/id were already captured into the closed-over `PlaybackState` at start, so an in-flight animation can safely finish using its own snapshot even if the path element is deleted from the scene concurrently — no special-casing needed beyond the target-deletion check above. (If the user wants deletion of the path to also abort playback immediately, that's a one-line addition: check `scene.getElement(pathId)` each tick similarly to the target check.)
- **Point-editing the path while an animation targeting it is in-flight**: because `PlaybackState.pathPoints` is captured once at `start()` and never re-read from the live element, an in-progress animation is **unaffected by concurrent edits** to the path's points — it finishes playing out the geometry as it was at trigger time. This is a reasonable, low-surprise default (consistent with "no scrubbing/live state" scope) and needs no special locking/guard code; just confirm this is acceptable to the user rather than, say, wanting edits to immediately cancel in-flight playback (which would require the tick to re-check `scene.getElement(path.id).points !== capturedPoints` and early-return `null` if changed — a small addition if the user prefers it).

## 7. Interface needed from the path element data model

Confirmed as matching: `targetElementId: string | null` XOR `targetGroupId: GroupId | null`, `points: readonly LocalPoint[]` local to the path's own `x`/`y` (same convention as `ExcalidrawLinearElement.points`, `packages/element/src/types.ts:340-343`).

**Missing / needed, not currently planned by the other track — specify here:**

- `getPathLength(points: readonly LocalPoint[]): number` and `getPointAtProgress(points: readonly LocalPoint[], t: number): { x: number; y: number }` — a small new utility module. Recommend `packages/element/src/path.ts` (co-located with `getPathTargetElements` from §2, and wherever the data-model plan puts the path element's own geometry helpers — reconcile file location with that plan to avoid two competing "path.ts" files). Built on `pointDistance` from `packages/math/src/point.ts:195` for segment lengths; `getPointAtProgress` walks cumulative segment length to find which segment contains `t * totalLength`, then linearly interpolates within that segment. No existing polyline arc-length utility exists in the codebase to reuse (confirmed via search) — this must be written new, but it's genuinely small (~20-30 lines) and has no other dependencies.
- **One semantic clarification needed from the data-model plan**: does `points[0]` represent the target's position _at path-creation time_ (i.e., should playback snap the target to the path's absolute start before animating), or is the path purely a shape describing a relative offset sequence to be applied from wherever the target currently sits? This plan assumes the latter (§3's `dx - startDx` delta-based approach, which moves the target _relative to its own current position_ by however the path's shape displaces over time, regardless of where the path geometrically sits on the canvas or where the target currently is). This is more robust (works even if the target has been moved since the path was drawn) but should be confirmed against the other plan's intended semantics before implementation, since if the other design intends the path's absolute coordinates to matter (e.g., a path literally overlaid on the canvas that the element should visibly trace), the interpolation math changes from "relative delta from `points[0]`" to "absolute `path.x + point.x`, `path.y + point.y`."

### Critical Files for Implementation

- packages/excalidraw/renderer/animation.ts — existing shared `AnimationController`, reused as the single driver for all concurrent path playbacks
- packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx — pointer gesture hook-in (~lines 733, 755-756, 8356-8397, 8895-8976, drag/pointerup precedents at 11001/11246/11490), new `pathPlayback`/`pathPlaybackArmTimer` fields
- packages/excalidraw/pathPlayback.ts (new) — `PathPlaybackController`, per-path animation state machine, `CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER` scheduling
- packages/element/src/path.ts (new, reconcile name/location with the data-model plan) — `getPathTargetElements`, `getPathLength`, `getPointAtProgress`
- packages/element/src/Scene.ts — `mutateElement` (line 411) and `getElementsFromId` (line 397) reused as-is for mutation and target/group resolution
- packages/element/src/store.ts — `CaptureUpdateAction` semantics (`IMMEDIATELY`/`NEVER`/`EVENTUALLY`) that govern undo-history safety during per-frame mutation

<result># Motion Path — Playback/Animation Mechanism: Implementation Plan

This plan covers only the trigger gesture, the animation driver, element mutation, and state lifecycle. It treats the `"path"` element type, `targetElementId`/`targetGroupId`, and `points: readonly LocalPoint[]` as a given interface from the parallel data-model plan.

## 0. Key discoveries that shape the design

- **A generic, keyed, shared animation driver already exists**: `packages/excalidraw/renderer/animation.ts` — `AnimationController`. It supports multiple concurrently-running, independently-keyed animations off a single RAF (or `setTimeout` fallback when render-throttling is disabled), each with its own per-tick `state` and `deltaTime`. It's already used for viewport fly-to animation (`packages/excalidraw/viewport.ts`, key `SCROLL_TO_CONTENT_ANIMATION_KEY`) and the laser/eraser trails (`packages/excalidraw/animatedTrail.ts`). **This is exactly the mechanism needed for concurrent path playback — do not build a second RAF loop.** Use `AnimationController.start(key, animation)` / `.cancel(key)` / `.running(key)`.
- **Ephemeral, non-persisted "runtime" state belongs on the `App` class instance, not in `appState`.** Precedent: `laserTrails = new LaserTrails(this)` and `eraserTrail = new EraserTrail(this)` at `packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx:755-756`, and `private bindModeHandler: ReturnType&lt;typeof setTimeout&gt; | null = null;` (~line 733) for an armed "hold" timer. Every `appState` key must additionally be registered in `APP_STATE_STORAGE_CONF` in `packages/excalidraw/appState.ts` (all `false` by default) for `clearAppStateForLocalStorage`/export/database filtering — adding a new appState key is strictly more ceremony than a class field for something that must never persist, never undo, and never diff against `ObservedAppState`. **Recommendation: a plain `App` class field**, not appState.
- **`CaptureUpdateAction` only controls undo/redo capture — it does not stop `onChange`.** `componentDidUpdate` (App.tsx ~3694-3703) calls `this.store.commit(...)` _and_ `this.props.onChange?.(...)` on every render, unconditionally. `CaptureUpdateAction` (`packages/element/src/store.ts`) governs only what `store.commit` does with the diff (`IMMEDIATELY` → pushed to undo stack now; `EVENTUALLY` → deferred/merged into the next `IMMEDIATELY`; `NEVER` → discarded, never recorded). The default when nothing is scheduled this tick is `EVENTUALLY` (`store.ts` `getScheduledMacroAction`).
- **The existing drag-to-move flow is the precedent for "many per-frame mutations → one undo entry."** During pointermove, `dragSelectedElements` (`packages/element/src/dragElements.ts`) calls `scene.mutateElement` repeatedly with no explicit capture scheduling (falls through to default `EVENTUALLY`); on pointerup, `this.store.scheduleCapture()` is called exactly once (e.g. `App.tsx:11001`, `:11246`, `:11490`) to collapse the whole gesture into a single `IMMEDIATELY` history entry. Other one-off "discard this mutation" sites explicitly call `this.store.scheduleAction(CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER)` (e.g. `App.tsx:12223`, `:8080`, `:3127`, `:11321`, `:11499`) — this is the idiom to copy for "this mutation must never be undoable."
- **Group → elements resolution already exists and is reused elsewhere**: `Scene.getElementsFromId(id)` (`packages/element/src/Scene.ts:397-407`) does precisely "if `id` is an element id, return `[element]`; otherwise treat it as a group id and call `getElementsInGroup(elementsMap, id)`" (`packages/element/src/groups.ts:289`). This is a direct match for resolving `targetElementId ?? targetGroupId` to a concrete element list — no new resolution logic needed.
- **Rigid-body group translation precedent**: `dragSelectedElements`/`updateElementCoords` in `packages/element/src/dragElements.ts:204-220` — captures each element's _original_ `x`/`y` (from `pointerDownState.originalElements`), then every tick sets `x = originalX + offset.x`, `y = originalY + offset.y` via `scene.mutateElement`. This is simpler than reusing the function wholesale (it's entangled with `PointerDownState`, snapping, elbow-arrow rebinding, frame membership) — the plan below extracts just the "capture original positions once, translate by a delta every tick" shape of it, not the function itself.
- **No existing long-press/hold helper.** The closest precedent is `bindModeHandler` (a raw `setTimeout` id stored as a nullable class field, armed/cleared directly in pointer handlers) — follow that pattern rather than introducing a generic hook.
- **No existing polyline length/arc-length utility** (expected, since the `path` element doesn't exist yet). A small new module is needed (detailed in §7).

## 1. Press-and-hold gesture detection

**Where it hooks in:** `packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx`, inside the existing pointerdown handler for the `"selection"` tool (the branch guarded by `this.state.activeTool.type === "selection"`, where `pointerDownState.hit.element` is already resolved — see assignments around `App.tsx:8895-8976`). This runs regardless of what else selection-mode pointerdown does (selecting/preparing to drag); it does not require a new tool.

**New `App` class fields** (next to `bindModeHandler`, ~line 733):

```ts
private pathPlaybackArmTimer: ReturnType&lt;typeof setTimeout&gt; | null = null;
private pathPlaybackArmedAt: { x: number; y: number } | null = null; // pointerdown coords, for move-threshold check
```

**Logic, added at the end of the existing pointerdown selection branch** (near `App.tsx:8356`, right after the current hit/selection bookkeeping, as a new private method `private armPathPlaybackIfApplicable(pointerDownState, hitElement)`):

1. Resolve whether `hitElement` has an associated path. This requires one new read-only lookup supplied by (or added alongside) the data-model plan: `scene.getPathForTarget(elementId)` or equivalent — scanning scene elements for a `"path"` element whose `targetElementId === hitElement.id` or whose `targetGroupId` is one of `hitElement.groupIds`. If none, do nothing (plain selection/drag proceeds untouched).
2. If found and no animation is already running for this path (see §6 "already mid-animation" below), arm: `this.pathPlaybackArmedAt = { x: pointerDownState.origin.x, y: pointerDownState.origin.y }` and `this.pathPlaybackArmTimer = setTimeout(() =&gt; this.startPathPlayback(path, hitElement), PATH_PLAYBACK_HOLD_MS)` where `PATH_PLAYBACK_HOLD_MS = 1000` is a new constant (co-located with `DRAGGING_THRESHOLD` in `packages/common/src/constants.ts`, or locally in App.tsx next to `BIND_MODE_TIMEOUT` if that constant's module is more appropriate — match whichever module `BIND_MODE_TIMEOUT` lives in).

**Cancellation (mirrors `bindModeHandler`'s clear sites and the `DRAGGING_THRESHOLD`-based cancel at `App.tsx:6980`):**

- **On pointermove**, in the existing generic pointermove handler (same place that computes `draggedDistance` / handles `DRAGGING_THRESHOLD`, ~`App.tsx:1444` pattern, or the per-gesture pointermove branch that follows pointerdown): if `this.pathPlaybackArmTimer` is set and the move distance from `pathPlaybackArmedAt` exceeds `DRAGGING_THRESHOLD` (same constant already imported, `packages/common/src/constants.ts:19`, value `10`px), call `clearTimeout(this.pathPlaybackArmTimer); this.pathPlaybackArmTimer = null;`. This is what lets a normal drag-to-move proceed unimpeded — if the user is actually dragging, the gesture naturally exceeds 10px well before 1000ms and the long-press is cancelled, so there is no conflict with drag-to-move.
- **On pointerup** (top of the existing `onPointerUp`/`handlePointerUp`, unconditionally, before any other branching): same clear. This is what lets a normal quick click/selection proceed unimpeded — if the user releases before 1000ms, the timer never fires, selection behaves exactly as today.
- **On pointer leaving the canvas / pointercancel**: same clear, added to the existing `pointerleave`/blur handlers used for other armed timers/drags.
- A long-press that _does_ fire (full 1000ms held without exceeding the move threshold) should **not** additionally trigger the normal click/select/drag outcome for that pointerdown — set a `pointerDownState.hit.wasPathPlaybackTriggered = true`-style flag (or simply check `this.pathPlaybackArmTimer === null &amp;&amp; &lt;animation started&gt;` at the top of pointerup) so pointerup's normal "this was a click" logic short-circuits. Concretely: once `startPathPlayback` fires, null out `this.pathPlaybackArmTimer` and set a transient flag read once by the pointerup handler to skip the click-selection branch for that gesture (selection itself — the element becoming selected — can still be allowed to stand; only "click toggled selection a second time" / "treated as a completed short click" needs suppressing). This needs a small, explicit one-off boolean rather than reusing `pointerDownState.hit.wasAddedToSelection`, to avoid coupling to unrelated selection semantics.

**No new generic "long-press hook" abstraction** — per the project's existing convention (raw `setTimeout` id as a class field, `bindModeHandler`), this is implemented as two class fields and ~15 lines across pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup, not a reusable hook.

## 2. Resolving target(s) to move

New function, colocated with other path-specific geometry (either a new `packages/element/src/path.ts`, or appended to wherever the data-model plan already puts path-specific helpers — confirm file name with that plan):

```ts
// packages/element/src/path.ts
export const getPathTargetElements = (
  scene: Scene,
  path: ExcalidrawPathElement,
): NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[] =&gt; {
  const id = path.targetElementId ?? path.targetGroupId;
  if (!id) return [];
  return scene.getElementsFromId(id); // already handles "element id" vs "group id" uniformly
};
```

This is a thin wrapper — `Scene.getElementsFromId` (`packages/element/src/Scene.ts:397-407`) already does the element-vs-group disambiguation and calls `getElementsInGroup` (`packages/element/src/groups.ts:289`) for the group case. No new group-membership logic is written.

Also resolve and move each target's **bound text element**, mirroring `dragSelectedElements`'s handling (`getBoundTextElement(element, elementsMap)`, `packages/element/src/textElement.ts`) — if a target (or a group member) is a container with bound text, the text must translate with it or it will visually detach during playback.

## 3. Animation loop design

**Driver:** `AnimationController` (`packages/excalidraw/renderer/animation.ts`) — one `AnimationController.start(key, animation)` call per triggered path, keyed by e.g. `` `path-playback-${path.id}` ``. Multiple concurrent triggers simply register multiple keys; `AnimationController` already multiplexes them over its single shared scheduled frame (`tick()` iterates `AnimationController.animations` each frame — `animation.ts:84-116`), satisfying the "Multiple Path" concurrency requirement with zero new scheduling code.

**New module**: `packages/excalidraw/pathPlayback.ts` (new file, App-adjacent like `animatedTrail.ts`), exporting a small `PathPlaybackController` class instantiated once on `App` (`pathPlayback = new PathPlaybackController(this)`, next to `laserTrails`/`eraserTrail` at `App.tsx:755-756`).

```ts
type PlaybackState = {
  elapsed: number;           // ms
  totalDuration: number;     // ms, computed once at start
  pathId: string;
  originalPositions: Map&lt;string, { x: number; y: number }&gt;; // targetId -&gt; original x/y
  pathPoints: readonly LocalPoint[];
};

class PathPlaybackController {
  constructor(private app: App) {}

  start(path: ExcalidrawPathElement, targets: NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[]) {
    const key = `path-playback-${path.id}`;
    if (AnimationController.running(key)) return; // see §6 "restart vs ignore"

    const length = getPathLength(path.points);
    const totalDuration = (length / PATH_PLAYBACK_SPEED_PX_PER_SEC) * 1000;
    const originalPositions = new Map(
      targets.map((el) =&gt; [el.id, { x: el.x, y: el.y }]),
    );

    AnimationController.start&lt;PlaybackState&gt;(key, ({ deltaTime, state }) =&gt; {
      const next: PlaybackState = state
        ? { ...state, elapsed: state.elapsed + deltaTime }
        : { elapsed: 0, totalDuration, pathId: path.id, originalPositions, pathPoints: path.points };

      const t = Math.min(next.elapsed / next.totalDuration, 1);
      const { x: dx, y: dy } = getPointAtProgress(next.pathPoints, t);
      const { x: startDx, y: startDy } = next.pathPoints[0];

      for (const target of targets) {
        const orig = next.originalPositions.get(target.id)!;
        this.app.scene.mutateElement(
          target,
          { x: orig.x + (dx - startDx), y: orig.y + (dy - startDy) },
          { informMutation: true, isDragging: true },
        );
      }
      this.app.store.scheduleAction(CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER); // never undoable per-frame

      if (t &gt;= 1) {
        this.finish(path.id, targets, next.originalPositions);
        return null; // AnimationController deregisters the key
      }
      return next;
    });
  }

  private finish(pathId, targets, originalPositions) {
    // see §5 for end-of-animation behavior
  }

  cancel(pathId: string) { AnimationController.cancel(`path-playback-${pathId}`); }
}
```

Notes on this design:

- **Constant speed, not fixed duration** — `PATH_PLAYBACK_SPEED_PX_PER_SEC` (new constant, recommend **300px/sec** as a starting default, tunable without redesign) is computed against the path's total length (`getPathLength`, §7) once at start, giving `totalDuration`. This satisfies "fixed, consistent base speed" (decision #3) while naturally giving longer paths longer playback — more intuitive than a fixed duration where a long path would suddenly move very fast relative to a short one. (A fixed-duration alternative is one constant away — `totalDuration = 1000` instead of length/speed — if the user prefers that; flagging as a one-line decision, not an architecture fork.)
- **Linear interpolation along the ordered point sequence, not just a straight line from start to end** — `getPointAtProgress` (§7) must walk the segments by cumulative length so the element visibly follows every vertex of the path, not just interpolate between the first and last point.
- **Per-frame capture is explicitly `NEVER`, every tick**, not left to default `EVENTUALLY`. This is deliberately stronger than the drag precedent: with drag, nothing else is likely to schedule `IMMEDIATELY` mid-gesture, so relying on default `EVENTUALLY` + a single terminal `scheduleCapture()` is safe. With animation, the gesture can run for a few seconds, during which _unrelated_ user actions (e.g., editing a different element) could call `scheduleCapture()` first — since `getScheduledMacroAction` gives `IMMEDIATELY` precedence over any pending `EVENTUALLY`, that would sweep the moving element's current mid-flight frame into the user's unrelated undo entry. Explicitly scheduling `NEVER` every tick avoids that entirely (consistent with how `NEVER` is used elsewhere for "this specific mutation must never be recorded," e.g. `App.tsx:12223`, `:8080`).
- **`isDragging: true`** passed to `mutateElement`'s options mirrors how drag/bind-mode-style continuous repositioning already flags itself (see `App.tsx:1280-1292` and `dragElements.ts`), rather than inventing a new option value.
- **One shared RAF per frame drives all concurrent playbacks**, and because React 18 batches `setState` calls issued synchronously within one callback, multiple targets' `mutateElement` calls inside the same `AnimationController.tick()` invocation collapse into a single re-render (`Scene.triggerUpdate` → `App.triggerRender` → `this.setState({})`) regardless of how many paths are animating that frame.

**Known residual concern — collab/localStorage write frequency**: `componentDidUpdate` calls `this.props.onChange` on every re-render **regardless of `CaptureUpdateAction`** (`App.tsx:3694-3703`). In `excalidraw-app/App.tsx:679-734`, `onChange` synchronously calls `collabAPI.syncElements(elements)` → `Collab.tsx:954` `broadcastElements` with no throttle, and schedules a `LocalData.save`. A ~60fps (or even throttled ~24-30fps) playback will therefore still cause one `onChange`/broadcast per rendered frame while any path is playing. This is **not fixable from within `packages/excalidraw` alone** — it's a property of the host app's `onChange` handler. Two mitigations, neither required for this issue but worth flagging for the user:

1. Throttle the playback tick itself (e.g. target ~30fps instead of every RAF frame, using the `deltaTime` `AnimationController` already supplies — skip mutating until `elapsed since last mutate &gt;= ~33ms`), halving the broadcast rate for a still-smooth basic animation.
2. A follow-up (likely head issue #18 territory, since it touches collab) to make `excalidraw-app/collab/Collab.tsx`'s `broadcastElements` throttle-coalesce bursts of same-tick element updates, independent of this feature. I recommend doing (1) now (cheap, local, no cross-cutting change) and explicitly deferring (2).

---

## 4. Where playback state lives

**Recommendation: `App` class instance fields**, not `appState`. Concretely:

- `pathPlayback: PathPlaybackController` — instance of the new controller above, holding nothing persisted; its only state is what's inside `AnimationController`'s private `animations` map (keyed by path id), which itself is a `static` module-level map, not tied to React state/appState at all.
- `pathPlaybackArmTimer` / `pathPlaybackArmedAt` (§1) — tiny gesture-arming state, same category as `bindModeHandler`.

Reasoning, directly from the codebase's own convention: `appState` keys are either persisted-by-default or must be explicitly whitelisted per export target in `APP_STATE_STORAGE_CONF` (`packages/excalidraw/appState.ts:~200-266`), and are part of `ObservedAppState`/history delta comparisons (`packages/element/src/delta.ts`, `AppStateDelta`) — i.e., putting playback progress in `appState` would make it a candidate for diffing/observation machinery designed for user-facing, undo-relevant state. The two existing "ephemeral per-frame visual state" features (laser trail, eraser trail) both avoid `appState` entirely and live as plain class fields (`App.tsx:755-756`) wrapping their own internal mutable state (`AnimatedTrail`'s `currentTrail`/`pastTrails`, in `packages/excalidraw/animatedTrail.ts`) — this feature matches that shape closely enough to copy it directly rather than inventing a third pattern.

---

## 5. End-of-animation behavior (needs user confirmation — flagging as an open decision)

Two reasonable options:

- **Option A — snap back to the pre-animation position (recommended).** `finish()` restores `target.x/y` to the captured `originalPositions` for every target, then calls `this.app.store.scheduleAction(CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER)` once more (net position change across the whole gesture is zero, so there is nothing meaningful to make undoable, and no stray entry risks confusing `Ctrl+Z`). This matches the "press-and-hold to **preview** motion" framing of the trigger gesture — it behaves like a repeatable preview/demo rather than a destructive edit, is safe to trigger accidentally or repeatedly, and keeps the element's canonical diagram position exactly as the user placed it regardless of how many times playback runs. It also sidesteps needing to decide what "redo the same animation after it ended at the destination" should even mean for a second trigger.
- **Option B — leave the element at the path's end.** `finish()` does nothing further (element stays wherever the last frame left it), and calls `this.app.store.scheduleCapture()` once (so the whole displacement from start → end collapses into exactly one `IMMEDIATELY` undo entry, same as a normal drag). This matches tools like PowerPoint's default motion-path behavior (object stays at the path's end after the effect plays) and may be what users expect if they're using the path to permanently reposition an element via "play."

**I recommend Option A** given the "press-and-hold to trigger, no scrubbing/transport controls" framing suggests a preview-style interaction rather than an editing action, and because it composes more simply with "trigger again" (§6) — but this is explicitly a product decision, not an architectural one, and should be confirmed with the user before implementation. The code difference between the two is isolated entirely to the ~6-line `finish()` method.

---

## 6. Edge cases

- **Re-triggering an already-animating target**: `PathPlaybackController.start()` checks `AnimationController.running(key)` and currently **ignores** the new trigger if already running (simplest, avoids visual popping from restarting mid-flight). An alternative ("restart from the top") is a one-line change — `AnimationController.cancel(key)` before `.start()` — flagging this as a minor, easy-to-swap decision alongside §5, not a structural one. Recommend **ignore** to start, since it's the conservative default and restart is strictly easier to add later than to remove the cancel-and-rerun semantics once users depend on it.
- **Target element deleted mid-animation**: each tick, before mutating, filter `targets` to currently-non-deleted elements (`!this.app.scene.getElement(id)?.isDeleted`); if the _entire_ target set becomes empty, return `null` from the `AnimationController` callback immediately (ending the animation early, no `finish()` repositioning needed since there's nothing left to reposition). This requires re-resolving via `scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap()` each tick rather than closing over a stale array, since the Scene mutates in place.
- **Path element deleted mid-animation**: the path's `points`/id were already captured into the closed-over `PlaybackState` at start, so an in-flight animation can safely finish using its own snapshot even if the path element is deleted from the scene concurrently — no special-casing needed beyond the target-deletion check above. (If the user wants deletion of the path to also abort playback immediately, that's a one-line addition: check `scene.getElement(pathId)` each tick similarly to the target check.)
- **Point-editing the path while an animation targeting it is in-flight**: because `PlaybackState.pathPoints` is captured once at `start()` and never re-read from the live element, an in-progress animation is **unaffected by concurrent edits** to the path's points — it finishes playing out the geometry as it was at trigger time. This is a reasonable, low-surprise default (consistent with "no scrubbing/live state" scope) and needs no special locking/guard code; just confirm this is acceptable to the user rather than, say, wanting edits to immediately cancel in-flight playback (which would require the tick to re-check `scene.getElement(path.id).points !== capturedPoints` and early-return `null` if changed — a small addition if the user prefers it).

## 7. Interface needed from the path element data model

Confirmed as matching: `targetElementId: string | null` XOR `targetGroupId: GroupId | null`, `points: readonly LocalPoint[]` local to the path's own `x`/`y` (same convention as `ExcalidrawLinearElement.points`, `packages/element/src/types.ts:340-343`).

**Missing / needed, not currently planned by the other track — specify here:**

- `getPathLength(points: readonly LocalPoint[]): number` and `getPointAtProgress(points: readonly LocalPoint[], t: number): { x: number; y: number }` — a small new utility module. Recommend `packages/element/src/path.ts` (co-located with `getPathTargetElements` from §2, and wherever the data-model plan puts the path element's own geometry helpers — reconcile file location with that plan to avoid two competing "path.ts" files). Built on `pointDistance` from `packages/math/src/point.ts:195` for segment lengths; `getPointAtProgress` walks cumulative segment length to find which segment contains `t * totalLength`, then linearly interpolates within that segment. No existing polyline arc-length utility exists in the codebase to reuse (confirmed via search) — this must be written new, but it's genuinely small (~20-30 lines) and has no other dependencies.
- **One semantic clarification needed from the data-model plan**: does `points[0]` represent the target's position _at path-creation time_ (i.e., should playback snap the target to the path's absolute start before animating), or is the path purely a shape describing a relative offset sequence to be applied from wherever the target currently sits? This plan assumes the latter (§3's `dx - startDx` delta-based approach, which moves the target _relative to its own current position_ by however the path's shape displaces over time, regardless of where the path geometrically sits on the canvas or where the target currently is). This is more robust (works even if the target has been moved since the path was drawn) but should be confirmed against the other plan's intended semantics before implementation, since if the other design intends the path's absolute coordinates to matter (e.g., a path literally overlaid on the canvas that the element should visibly trace), the interpolation math changes from "relative delta from `points[0]`" to "absolute `path.x + point.x`, `path.y + point.y`."

**When the press-and-hold animation finishes playing, where should the element end up?**

Options:

- **Snap back to original position (Recommended)** - Element returns to exactly where it was before playback started. Treats the long-press as a repeatable 'preview' of the motion — safe to trigger repeatedly or by accident, no undo entry is created since nothing net-changes.
- **Stay at the path's end position** - Element remains wherever the path's last point left it, as one single undo-able move (like a drag). Matches how motion-path effects in presentation tools usually behave — the element is actually relocated.

**If the user long-presses an element that's already mid-animation along its path, what should happen?**

Options:

- **Ignore the new trigger (Recommended)** - The in-progress animation keeps playing untouched; the new long-press has no effect until the current one finishes. Simplest, avoids visual popping.
- **Restart from the beginning** - Cancel the in-progress animation and immediately start a fresh one from t=0.

**Answer:** Snap back to original position (Recommended), Ignore the new trigger (Recommended)

````markdown
# Issue #45 — Motion Path Tool

## Context

Issue #45 (head issue #18, "Allow elements to have motion") asks for a way to define a path that a selected element — or a group of elements — can follow. The user should be able to draw a path with a start point, an end point, and optional midpoints from a dedicated toolbar tool, have that path persist with its configured point positions, and then trigger a basic motion preview by pressing and holding the associated element.

Scope agreed with the user before this plan was written:

- The path is a **new first-class element type** (`"path"`), not a repurposed line — but it reuses as much of the existing multi-point line drawing/editing machinery as practical.
- Association to a target element or native group is **fixed at creation time** (stored on the path, not re-targetable afterwards).
- **Basic, fixed-speed playback is in scope for this issue** (press-and-hold ~1s on the target → element slides along the path at a constant speed, every time, no easing/ timing configuration). Configurable speed/timing/easing and persisted playback state are explicitly out of scope and deferred to head issue #18.
- Multiple independent paths, each targeting a different element/group, must coexist and be able to play back concurrently.
- End-of-animation: the element **snaps back to its original position** (the long-press is a repeatable preview, not a destructive move).
- Re-triggering a path that's already mid-animation is **ignored** until it finishes.

This plan covers: the `path` element type, the toolbar tool and its two-phase creation flow (pick target → draw points → confirm), post-creation point editing, minimal rendering/restore/bounds support, and the press-and-hold playback mechanism. It does not cover persisted animation timelines, speed/easing configuration, or playback transport controls — those belong to issue #18.

## Data model

**`packages/element/src/types.ts`** — add a new element type sibling to `ExcalidrawLinearElement`, not folded into it (paths don't bind, don't have arrowheads, and keeping them structurally separate avoids auditing every `isLinearElement` call site for binding/arrowhead behavior):

export type ExcalidrawPathElement = _ExcalidrawElementBase &
  Readonly<{
    type: "path";
    points: readonly LocalPoint[];
    /** mutually exclusive; resolved once at creation time, never re-targeted */
    targetElementId: string | null;
    targetGroupId: GroupId | null;
  }>;
```

Add `ExcalidrawPathElement` to the `ExcalidrawElement` union (`types.ts:211-221`).

If multiple paths ever target the same element, only the first one found plays on a given long-press (prevents two animations fighting over the same element's `x`/`y` each frame); creating more than one is still allowed, just not simultaneously playable.

**Edge cases (apply uniformly, no special-case code beyond what's listed):**

## Press-and-hold playback

**Reuse the existing shared animation driver** — `AnimationController` in `packages/excalidraw/renderer/animation.ts` already supports multiple concurrently-keyed animations off a single RAF loop (used today by viewport fly-to and the laser/eraser trails). Do not build a second RAF loop.

**New module `packages/excalidraw/pathPlayback.ts`** (App-adjacent, like `animatedTrail.ts`), exporting `PathPlaybackController`, instantiated once as an `App` class field (`this.pathPlayback = new PathPlaybackController(this)`, next to `laserTrails`/`eraserTrail`):

```ts
start(path: ExcalidrawPathElement, targets: NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[]) {
  const key = `path-playback-${path.id}`;
  if (AnimationController.running(key)) return; // ignore re-trigger while playing

  const length = getPathLength(path.points);
  const totalDuration = (length / PATH_PLAYBACK_SPEED_PX_PER_SEC) * 1000; // 300px/s default
  const originalPositions = new Map(targets.map((el) => [el.id, { x: el.x, y: el.y }]));

  AnimationController.start(key, ({ deltaTime, state }) => {
    const next = state ? { ...state, elapsed: state.elapsed + deltaTime }
                       : { elapsed: 0, totalDuration, originalPositions };
    const t = Math.min(next.elapsed / next.totalDuration, 1);
    const { x: dx, y: dy } = getPointAtProgress(path.points, t);
    const { x: startDx, y: startDy } = path.points[0];

    const liveTargets = targets.filter((el) => !this.app.scene.getElement(el.id)?.isDeleted);
    if (liveTargets.length === 0) return null; // all targets gone — end early

    for (const target of liveTargets) {
      const orig = next.originalPositions.get(target.id)!;
      this.app.scene.mutateElement(target, {
        x: orig.x + (dx - startDx),
        y: orig.y + (dy - startDy),
      }, { isDragging: true });
    }
    this.app.store.scheduleAction(CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER); // never undoable, every tick

    if (t >= 1) {
      // snap back: restore original positions, still never-undoable
      for (const target of liveTargets) {
        const orig = next.originalPositions.get(target.id)!;
        this.app.scene.mutateElement(target, orig);
      }
      this.app.store.scheduleAction(CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER);
      return null;
    }
    return next;
  });
}
```

Key points:

- **Constant speed (px/sec), not fixed duration** — `PATH_PLAYBACK_SPEED_PX_PER_SEC` (new constant, default 300) is combined with the path's own length (`getPathLength`) so longer paths naturally take longer, rather than moving faster to fit a fixed time.
- **Relative-delta motion, not absolute path coordinates** — the target moves by however much the path's shape displaces from `points[0]` at progress `t`, applied as an offset from the target's own captured original position. This works regardless of where the path sits on canvas relative to the target, and regardless of whether the target has moved since the path was drawn.
- **`CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER` scheduled explicitly on every tick** (not left to the default `EVENTUALLY`) — stronger than the normal drag precedent, because an animation can run for seconds, during which an unrelated user action elsewhere could schedule an `IMMEDIATELY` capture that would otherwise sweep a mid-flight animation frame into an unrelated undo entry.
- **Bound text / group members move with their container/group**, same as drag-to-move (`packages/element/src/dragElements.ts` is the precedent to check for bound-text handling via `getBoundTextElement`).
- **Target resolution** goes through `scene.getElementsFromId(id)` (`packages/element/src/Scene.ts:397-407`), which already disambiguates an element id from a group id and returns the live member list — no new group-membership logic.

**Press-and-hold gesture** — `packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx`, hooked into the existing `"selection"`-tool pointer-down branch (not a new tool; works on ordinary selection-mode clicks), two new class fields next to the existing `bindModeHandler` precedent:

```ts
private pathPlaybackArmTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
private pathPlaybackArmedAt: { x: number; y: number } | null = null;
```

- On pointerdown over an element: look up `getPathsTargetingElement(hitElement, elements)`; if non-empty and not already animating, arm a `setTimeout(..., 1000)` (new `PATH_PLAYBACK_HOLD_MS` constant) that calls `this.pathPlayback.start(path, getPathTargetElements(scene, path))` when it fires.
- Clear the timer (and don't fire): on pointermove once movement exceeds the existing `DRAGGING_THRESHOLD` (so a real drag-to-move is never intercepted — it naturally exceeds the threshold well before 1s), on pointerup, and on pointerleave/pointercancel.
- If the hold _does_ fire, suppress that pointer gesture's normal "completed click" handling on the subsequent pointerup (a one-off boolean flag, not a reuse of unrelated selection-state fields) — selection itself can stand, just don't double-toggle it.

**Where playback state lives** — plain `App` class instance fields (`pathPlayback`, `pathPlaybackArmTimer`, `pathPlaybackArmedAt`), not `appState`. This matches the existing precedent for ephemeral, non-persisted, non-undo-tracked runtime state (`laserTrails`/`eraserTrail` are instantiated the same way at `App.tsx:755-756`) — putting it in `appState` would require registering it in `APP_STATE_STORAGE_CONF` and would make it a candidate for history-delta comparison machinery that doesn't apply to it.

**Known follow-up, not required for this issue**: `componentDidUpdate` calls `this.props.onChange` on every re-render regardless of `CaptureUpdateAction`, so a playing animation will still cause one `onChange`/collab-broadcast per rendered frame. Throttling the playback tick itself to ~30fps (using the `deltaTime` `AnimationController` already provides) is a cheap, local mitigation worth including; a deeper fix to collab broadcast coalescing is out of scope and belongs with issue #18.
````

````text
## Approved Plan:
# Issue #45 — Motion Path Tool

## Context

Issue #45 (head issue #18, "Allow elements to have motion") asks for a way to define a
path that a selected element — or a group of elements — can follow. The user should be
able to draw a path with a start point, an end point, and optional midpoints from a
dedicated toolbar tool, have that path persist with its configured point positions, and
then trigger a basic motion preview by pressing and holding the associated element.

Scope agreed with the user before this plan was written:
- The path is a **new first-class element type** (`"path"`), not a repurposed line —
  but it reuses as much of the existing multi-point line drawing/editing machinery as
  practical.
- Association to a target element or native group is **fixed at creation time** (stored
  on the path, not re-targetable afterwards).
- **Basic, fixed-speed playback is in scope for this issue** (press-and-hold ~1s on the
  target → element slides along the path at a constant speed, every time, no easing/
  timing configuration). Configurable speed/timing/easing and persisted playback state
  are explicitly out of scope and deferred to head issue #18.
- Multiple independent paths, each targeting a different element/group, must coexist and
  be able to play back concurrently.
- End-of-animation: the element **snaps back to its original position** (the long-press
  is a repeatable preview, not a destructive move).
- Re-triggering a path that's already mid-animation is **ignored** until it finishes.

This plan covers: the `path` element type, the toolbar tool and its two-phase creation
flow (pick target → draw points → confirm), post-creation point editing, minimal
rendering/restore/bounds support, and the press-and-hold playback mechanism. It does not
cover persisted animation timelines, speed/easing configuration, or playback transport
controls — those belong to issue #18.
````

- **`packages/element/src/bounds.ts`** and **`packages/element/src/collision.ts`** — add `"path"` to the existing points-based bounds/hit-testing cases (`collision.ts`'s `intersectLinearOrFreeDrawWithLineSegment` grouping already works off `.points` alone and is a drop-in).
- **`packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts`** — matching dashed+dots case for SVG export parity (flag-level only; same visual treatment as the canvas renderer).

## Press-and-hold playback

**Reuse the existing shared animation driver** — `AnimationController` in `packages/excalidraw/renderer/animation.ts` already supports multiple concurrently-keyed animations off a single RAF loop (used today by viewport fly-to and the laser/eraser trails). Do not build a second RAF loop.

**New module `packages/excalidraw/pathPlayback.ts`** (App-adjacent, like `animatedTrail.ts`), exporting `PathPlaybackController`, instantiated once as an `App` class field (`this.pathPlayback = new PathPlaybackController(this)`, next to `laserTrails`/`eraserTrail`):

```ts
start(path: ExcalidrawPathElement, targets: NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[]) {
  const key = `path-playback-${path.id}`;
  if (AnimationController.running(key)) return; // ignore re-trigger while playing

  const length = getPathLength(path.points);
  const totalDuration = (length / PATH_PLAYBACK_SPEED_PX_PER_SEC) * 1000; // 300px/s default
  const originalPositions = new Map(targets.map((el) => [el.id, { x: el.x, y: el.y }]));

  AnimationController.start(key, ({ deltaTime, state }) => {
    const next = state ? { ...state, elapsed: state.elapsed + deltaTime }
                       : { elapsed: 0, totalDuration, originalPositions };
    const t = Math.min(next.elapsed / next.totalDuration, 1);
    const { x: dx, y: dy } = getPointAtProgress(path.points, t);
    const { x: startDx, y: startDy } = path.points[0];

    const liveTargets = targets.filter((el) => !this.app.scene.getElement(el.id)?.isDeleted);
    if (liveTargets.length === 0) return null; // all targets gone — end early

    for (const target of liveTargets) {
      const orig = next.originalPositions.get(target.id)!;
      this.app.scene.mutateElement(target, {
        x: orig.x + (dx - startDx),
        y: orig.y + (dy - startDy),
      }, { isDragging: true });
    }
    this.app.store.scheduleAction(CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER); // never undoable, every tick

    if (t >= 1) {
      // snap back: restore original positions, still never-undoable
      for (const target of liveTargets) {
        const orig = next.originalPositions.get(target.id)!;
        this.app.scene.mutateElement(target, orig);
      }
      this.app.store.scheduleAction(CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER);
      return null;
    }
    return next;
  });
}
```

Key points:

- **Constant speed (px/sec), not fixed duration** — `PATH_PLAYBACK_SPEED_PX_PER_SEC` (new constant, default 300) is combined with the path's own length (`getPathLength`) so longer paths naturally take longer, rather than moving faster to fit a fixed time.
- **Relative-delta motion, not absolute path coordinates** — the target moves by however much the path's shape displaces from `points[0]` at progress `t`, applied as an offset from the target's own captured original position. This works regardless of where the path sits on canvas relative to the target, and regardless of whether the target has moved since the path was drawn.
- **`CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER` scheduled explicitly on every tick** (not left to the default `EVENTUALLY`) — stronger than the normal drag precedent, because an animation can run for seconds, during which an unrelated user action elsewhere could schedule an `IMMEDIATELY` capture that would otherwise sweep a mid-flight animation frame into an unrelated undo entry.
- **Bound text / group members move with their container/group**, same as drag-to-move (`packages/element/src/dragElements.ts` is the precedent to check for bound-text handling via `getBoundTextElement`).
- **Target resolution** goes through `scene.getElementsFromId(id)` (`packages/element/src/Scene.ts:397-407`), which already disambiguates an element id from a group id and returns the live member list — no new group-membership logic.

**Press-and-hold gesture** — `packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx`, hooked into the existing `"selection"`-tool pointer-down branch (not a new tool; works on ordinary selection-mode clicks), two new class fields next to the existing `bindModeHandler` precedent:

```ts
private pathPlaybackArmTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
private pathPlaybackArmedAt: { x: number; y: number } | null = null;
```

- On pointerdown over an element: look up `getPathsTargetingElement(hitElement, elements)`; if non-empty and not already animating, arm a `setTimeout(..., 1000)` (new `PATH_PLAYBACK_HOLD_MS` constant) that calls `this.pathPlayback.start(path, getPathTargetElements(scene, path))` when it fires.
- Clear the timer (and don't fire): on pointermove once movement exceeds the existing `DRAGGING_THRESHOLD` (so a real drag-to-move is never intercepted — it naturally exceeds the threshold well before 1s), on pointerup, and on pointerleave/pointercancel.
- If the hold _does_ fire, suppress that pointer gesture's normal "completed click" handling on the subsequent pointerup (a one-off boolean flag, not a reuse of unrelated selection-state fields) — selection itself can stand, just don't double-toggle it.

**Where playback state lives** — plain `App` class instance fields (`pathPlayback`, `pathPlaybackArmTimer`, `pathPlaybackArmedAt`), not `appState`. This matches the existing precedent for ephemeral, non-persisted, non-undo-tracked runtime state (`laserTrails`/`eraserTrail` are instantiated the same way at `App.tsx:755-756`) — putting it in `appState` would require registering it in `APP_STATE_STORAGE_CONF` and would make it a candidate for history-delta comparison machinery that doesn't apply to it.

**Known follow-up, not required for this issue**: `componentDidUpdate` calls `this.props.onChange` on every re-render regardless of `CaptureUpdateAction`, so a playing animation will still cause one `onChange`/collab-broadcast per rendered frame. Throttling the playback tick itself to ~30fps (using the `deltaTime` `AnimationController` already provides) is a cheap, local mitigation worth including; a deeper fix to collab broadcast coalescing is out of scope and belongs with issue #18.

## Verification

1. **Type safety**: `yarn test:typecheck` must pass — this is also the authoritative way to discover every exhaustive-switch site that needs a `"path"` case.
2. **Unit tests** (`yarn test:update`): add cases to `packages/element/tests/linearElementEditor.test.tsx` for path point editing; add tests for `getPathLength`/`getPointAtProgress`/`getPathTargetElements`/ `getPathsTargetingElement` in a new `packages/element/tests/path.test.ts`.
3. **Manual verification in the running app** (`yarn start` or the dev build):
   - Draw a path: activate the Path tool from the overflow toolbar, click a rectangle, click 3+ points on the canvas, confirm with Enter — verify the path renders dashed with waypoint dots and persists its point positions after deselecting/reselecting.
   - Create a second path targeting a different element; verify both exist independently (acceptance criterion "Multiple Path").
   - Edit an existing path's points (double-click to enter edit mode, drag a point, add a midpoint) and verify positions retain correctly.
   - Select a group of 2+ elements, create a path targeting the group; verify `targetGroupId` resolves to all members.
   - Press and hold the target element (~1s): verify it animates along the path at a constant visual speed and snaps back to its original position at the end.
   - While an animation is playing, long-press the same element again: verify it's ignored until the first finishes.
   - Delete the path's target element/ungroup its target group, then observe the path renders with a muted/broken indicator and no longer triggers on long-press of anything.
   - Delete a path element directly; verify no errors and the (still-existing) target is unaffected.
   - Undo/redo after drawing and editing a path: verify path creation/edits are undoable, but no stray undo entries appear from playback itself.

```typescript
import { pointDistance } from "@excalidraw/math";

import { arrayToMap } from "@excalidraw/common";

import { getElementsInGroup } from "./groups";
import { isPathElement } from "./typeChecks";

import type { LocalPoint } from "@excalidraw/math";

import type {
  ElementsMapOrArray,
  ExcalidrawElement,
  ExcalidrawPathElement,
  NonDeletedExcalidrawElement,
} from "./types";

/**
 * Resolves a path's target to the concrete, currently-live element(s) it
 * should act on. `targetElementId` and `targetGroupId` are mutually
 * exclusive (enforced at creation time), so exactly one branch applies.
 * Returns an empty array once the target has been deleted/disbanded — the
 * path itself is left untouched (becomes inert) rather than being cleaned up.
 */
export const getPathTargetElements = (
  path: ExcalidrawPathElement,
  elements: ElementsMapOrArray,
): NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[] => {
  const elementsMap = arrayToMap(elements);

  if (path.targetElementId) {
    const element = elementsMap.get(path.targetElementId);
    return element && !element.isDeleted
      ? [element as NonDeletedExcalidrawElement]
      : [];
  }

  if (path.targetGroupId) {
    return getElementsInGroup(elementsMap, path.targetGroupId).filter(
      (element): element is NonDeletedExcalidrawElement => !element.isDeleted,
    );
  }

  return [];
};

/**
 * Reverse lookup: all path elements (among `elements`) that target the given
 * element, either directly or via a group it belongs to. If more than one
 * path targets the same element, callers that can only play one at a time
 * (press-and-hold playback) should use only the first entry.
 */
export const getPathsTargetingElement = (
  element: ExcalidrawElement,
  elements: ElementsMapOrArray,
): ExcalidrawPathElement[] => {
  const paths: ExcalidrawPathElement[] = [];
  for (const candidate of arrayToMap(elements).values()) {
    if (!isPathElement(candidate) || candidate.isDeleted) {
      continue;
    }
    if (
      candidate.targetElementId === element.id ||
      (candidate.targetGroupId !== null &&
        element.groupIds.includes(candidate.targetGroupId))
    ) {
      paths.push(candidate);
    }
  }
  return paths;
};

/** Total euclidean length of the polyline described by `points`. */
export const getPathLength = (points: readonly LocalPoint[]): number => {
  let length = 0;
  for (let i = 1; i < points.length; i++) {
    length += pointDistance(points[i - 1], points[i]);
  }
  return length;
};

/**
 * Walks the polyline's segments by cumulative length to find the point at
 * progress `t` (0..1) along it, interpolating within the containing segment.
 * `t` is clamped to [0, 1]; a path with fewer than 2 points returns its only
 * point (or the origin if empty).
 */
export const getPointAtProgress = (
  points: readonly LocalPoint[],
  t: number,
): { x: number; y: number } => {
  if (points.length === 0) {
    return { x: 0, y: 0 };
  }
  if (points.length === 1) {
    return { x: points[0][0], y: points[0][1] };
  }

  const clampedT = Math.min(Math.max(t, 0), 1);
  const totalLength = getPathLength(points);

  if (totalLength === 0) {
    return { x: points[0][0], y: points[0][1] };
  }

  const targetLength = clampedT * totalLength;
  let traveled = 0;

  for (let i = 1; i < points.length; i++) {
    const segmentLength = pointDistance(points[i - 1], points[i]);
    if (traveled + segmentLength >= targetLength || i === points.length - 1) {
      const segmentT =
        segmentLength === 0 ? 0 : (targetLength - traveled) / segmentLength;
      const [x0, y0] = points[i - 1];
      const [x1, y1] = points[i];
      return {
        x: x0 + (x1 - x0) * segmentT,
        y: y0 + (y1 - y0) * segmentT,
      };
    }
    traveled += segmentLength;
  }

  const last = points[points.length - 1];
  return { x: last[0], y: last[1] };
};
```

```text
1020	  const subpoints = [] as [number, number][];

1030	      pointDistance(points[i], prev) / 2,
1031	    );
1032
1033	    if (prevIsHorizontal) {
1034	      if (prev[0] < point[0]) {
1035	        // LEFT

1037	      } else {
1038	        // RIGHT

1040	      }

1042	      // UP

1065	  }
```

```text
7
8	export class AnimationController {
9	  private static scheduledFrame:
10	    | { id: ReturnType<typeof requestAnimationFrame>; type: "raf" }
11	    | { id: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>; type: "timeout" }
12	    | null = null;
13	  private static animations = new Map<
14	    string,
15	    {
16	      animation: Animation<any>;
17	      lastTime: number;
18	      state: any;
19	    }
20	  >();
21
22	  static start<R extends object>(key: string, animation: Animation<R>) {
23	    if (AnimationController.animations.has(key)) {
24	      return;
25	    }
26
27	    const initialState = animation({
28	      deltaTime: 0,
29	      state: undefined,
30	    });
31
32	    if (initialState) {
33	      AnimationController.animations.set(key, {
34	        animation,
35	        lastTime: 0,
36	        state: initialState,
37	      });
38
39	      AnimationController.scheduleNextFrame();
40	    }
41	  }
42
43	  private static scheduleNextFrame() {
44	    if (AnimationController.scheduledFrame) {
45	      return;
46	    }
47
48	    if (isRenderThrottlingEnabled()) {
49	      AnimationController.scheduledFrame = {
50	        id: requestAnimationFrame(AnimationController.tick),
51	        type: "raf",
52	      };
53	    } else {
54	      AnimationController.scheduledFrame = {
55	        id: setTimeout(AnimationController.tick, 0),
56	        type: "timeout",
57	      };
58	    }
59	  }
60
61	  private static cancelScheduledFrame() {
62	    if (!AnimationController.scheduledFrame) {
63	      return;
64	    }
65
66	    if (AnimationController.scheduledFrame.type === "raf") {
67	      cancelAnimationFrame(AnimationController.scheduledFrame.id);
68	    } else {
69	      clearTimeout(AnimationController.scheduledFrame.id);
70	    }
71
72	    AnimationController.scheduledFrame = null;
73	  }
74
75	  private static cancelScheduledFrameIfIdle() {
76	    if (AnimationController.animations.size > 0) {
77	      return false;
78	    }
79
80	    AnimationController.cancelScheduledFrame();
81	    return true;
82	  }
83
84	  private static tick() {
85	    AnimationController.scheduledFrame = null;
86
87	    if (AnimationController.animations.size > 0) {
88	      for (const [key, animation] of AnimationController.animations) {
89	        const now = performance.now();
90	        const deltaTime =
91	          animation.lastTime === 0 ? 0 : now - animation.lastTime;
92
93	        const state = animation.animation({
94	          deltaTime,
95	          state: animation.state,
96	        });
97
98	        if (!state) {
99	          AnimationController.animations.delete(key);
100
101	          if (AnimationController.cancelScheduledFrameIfIdle()) {
102	            return;
103	          }
104	        } else {
105	          animation.lastTime = now;
106	          animation.state = state;
107	        }
108	      }
109
110	      if (AnimationController.cancelScheduledFrameIfIdle()) {
111	        return;
112	      }
113
114	      AnimationController.scheduleNextFrame();
115	    }
116	  }
117
118	  static running(key: string) {
119	    return AnimationController.animations.has(key);
120	  }
121
122	  static cancel(key: string) {
123	    AnimationController.animations.delete(key);
124	    AnimationController.cancelScheduledFrameIfIdle();
125	  }
126
127	  static reset() {
128	    AnimationController.animations.clear();
129	    AnimationController.cancelScheduledFrame();
130	  }
131	}
```

```typescript
import {
  CaptureUpdateAction,
  getBoundTextElement,
  getPathLength,
  getPathTargetElements,
  getPointAtProgress,
} from "@excalidraw/element";

import { AnimationController } from "./renderer/animation";

import type {
  ExcalidrawPathElement,
  NonDeletedExcalidrawElement,
} from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import type App from "./components/App";

/** constant speed, not fixed duration — longer paths naturally take longer */
const PATH_PLAYBACK_SPEED_PX_PER_SEC = 300;

type PlaybackState = {
  elapsed: number;
  totalDuration: number;
  originalPositions: Map<string, { x: number; y: number }>;
};

/**
 * Drives the basic, fixed-speed "press and hold to preview" path animation.
 * Reuses the shared `AnimationController` (a single RAF loop multiplexing
 * every concurrently-keyed animation) rather than running its own loop, so
 * multiple paths can play back at once with no extra scheduling code.
 *
 * The target moves by however much the path's shape displaces from its
 * first point at progress `t`, applied as an offset from the target's own
 * position at trigger time — not by snapping to the path's absolute
 * coordinates. This works regardless of where the path sits on the canvas
 * relative to its target.
 *
 * Per-frame mutations are explicitly scheduled as `CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER`
 * on every tick (not left to the default `EVENTUALLY`), since an animation
 * can run for seconds, during which an unrelated user action could schedule
 * an `IMMEDIATELY` capture that would otherwise sweep a mid-flight frame into
 * an unrelated undo entry.
 */
export class PathPlaybackController {
  constructor(private app: App) {}

  isPlaying(path: ExcalidrawPathElement): boolean {
    return AnimationController.running(playbackKey(path.id));
  }

  start(path: ExcalidrawPathElement, targets: NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[]) {
    const key = playbackKey(path.id);

    if (AnimationController.running(key) || targets.length === 0) {
      return;
    }

    const length = getPathLength(path.points);
    const totalDuration = Math.max(
      (length / PATH_PLAYBACK_SPEED_PX_PER_SEC) * 1000,
      1,
    );

    const elementsMap = this.app.scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap();
    const originalPositions = new Map<string, { x: number; y: number }>();
    for (const target of targets) {
      originalPositions.set(target.id, { x: target.x, y: target.y });
      const boundText = getBoundTextElement(target, elementsMap);
      if (boundText) {
        originalPositions.set(boundText.id, {
          x: boundText.x,
          y: boundText.y,
        });
      }
    }

    AnimationController.start<PlaybackState>(key, ({ deltaTime, state }) => {
      const next: PlaybackState = state
        ? { ...state, elapsed: state.elapsed + deltaTime }
        : { elapsed: 0, totalDuration, originalPositions };

      const t = Math.min(next.elapsed / next.totalDuration, 1);
      const { x: dx, y: dy } = getPointAtProgress(path.points, t);
      const [startDx, startDy] = path.points[0] ?? [0, 0];

      const liveOriginalPositions = new Map(
        [...next.originalPositions].filter(([id]) =>
          this.app.scene.getNonDeletedElement(id),
        ),
      );

      if (liveOriginalPositions.size === 0) {
        return null;
      }

      for (const [id, orig] of liveOriginalPositions) {
        const element = this.app.scene.getNonDeletedElement(id);
        if (!element) {
          continue;
        }
        this.app.scene.mutateElement(
          element,
          {
            x: orig.x + (dx - startDx),
            y: orig.y + (dy - startDy),
          },
          { informMutation: true, isDragging: true },
        );
      }
      this.app.scheduleNeverCapture();

      if (t >= 1) {
        for (const [id, orig] of liveOriginalPositions) {
          const element = this.app.scene.getNonDeletedElement(id);
          if (element) {
            this.app.scene.mutateElement(element, orig, {
              informMutation: true,
              isDragging: false,
            });
          }
        }
        this.app.scheduleNeverCapture();
        return null;
      }

      return next;
    });
  }

  cancel(path: ExcalidrawPathElement) {
    AnimationController.cancel(playbackKey(path.id));
  }
}

const playbackKey = (pathId: string) => `path-playback-${pathId}`;

export { getPathTargetElements };
```

# Autonomous loop check

You're being invoked on a timer while the user is away or occupied. The point is to keep work moving forward without the user driving every step - finishing things they started, maintaining PRs they're building, catching problems before they come back to find them. You're a steward, not an initiator. The user set you loose on their work, and the value you provide comes from reliably advancing things they've already set in motion, not from finding new things to do.

The key tension to navigate: the user trusts you enough to run autonomously, but that trust is easily lost. Acting on what the conversation already established is safe and valuable. Inventing new work or making irreversible changes without clear authorization erodes trust fast. When you're unsure whether something falls into "continuing established work" or "inventing new work," lean toward the former only when the transcript provides clear evidence the user wanted it done. If you find yourself reaching for justifications about why a push is probably fine, that's a signal to wait.

## What to act on

The current conversation is your highest-signal source - re-read the transcript above, since everything there is something the user was actively engaged with. The strongest signal is an in-progress PR you've been building together: review comments to address and resolve, failing CI checks to diagnose (and re-enqueue if they're flakes), merge conflicts to fix. The goal is to get the PR into a state where it's ready to merge pending only human review - the user shouldn't come back to find a PR blocked on things you could have handled. After that, look for unfinished implementation where the last exchange left something half-done, and explicit "I'll also..." or "next I'll..." commitments the conversation made and didn't honor. Weaker but still real: dangling questions you could now answer, verification steps that were skipped, edge cases that were mentioned but not handled, and natural continuations that don't require new decisions.

If you find anything in this category, act on it - actually do the work, don't describe what could be done. Run the tests, don't say "you could run the tests." The whole point of autonomous operation is that work gets done while the user is away.

When the conversation transcript has nothing left, the current branch's pull/merge request on the user's SCM is the next-best place to look. This is maintenance work - valuable, but lower priority than continuing the user's active work. Find the PR/MR for the current branch via the SCM's CLI, then check three things: CI status, unresolved review threads, and whether the branch has fallen behind the base. For failing CI, pull the failing job's logs and diagnose before acting - flaky-shaped failures (timeout, runner died, transient network) can be re-enqueued; real failures need a reproduction and a minimal fix. For unresolved review threads, fetch the comment, address the feedback, push, and resolve the thread via, for example, the GitHub GraphQL `resolveReviewThread` mutation (or the equivalent for whichever SCM the project uses). Before pushing anything, check whether someone else has pushed to the branch while you were working - if so, rebase (don't merge) to keep history clean.

When CI is green, threads are clear, and there's idle time, sweeping the branch for issues is a good use of that time - bug-hunt or simplification passes catch problems before reviewers do, saving everyone a round-trip.

If everything is genuinely quiet - no conversation work, no PR maintenance - say so in one sentence and stop. No summary of what you checked, no list of what you might do later. The user will see your message in the transcript when they come back; three consecutive "nothing to do" results means you should scale back to a quick CI check and stop, not narrate.

## Repeated invocations

If you see earlier autonomous checks in this conversation, adjust your scope accordingly. If a previous check left a question the user hasn't answered, the cost of acting depends on reversibility: for reversible actions (local edits, running tests), make your best call and proceed; for irreversible ones (pushing, deleting, sending), keep waiting - the cost of acting wrongly on something irreversible is much higher than the cost of waiting one more cycle. If three or more consecutive checks have found nothing actionable, things are quiet - do one quick CI/threads check and stop in a single line. Repeated "nothing to do" messages clutter the transcript and waste the user's attention when they come back to review.

Read and analyze freely - understanding the state of things has no blast radius. Make edits and run tests when you're confident they continue established work. Commit and push only when you're clearly continuing something the user authorized, or when the work pattern makes the intent obvious - like fixing CI on a PR you've been building together.
