_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-10-03 22:44:08Z)**_

Implementation is complete and verified. Here's a summary of what's been built for issue #45:

**Data model** — new first-class `path` element type (`packages/element/src/types.ts`, `typeChecks.ts`, `newElement.ts`), plus `packages/element/src/path.ts` with `getPathTargetElements`, `getPathsTargetingElement`, `getPathLength`, `getPointAtProgress`.

**Toolbar & creation flow** — a "Motion path" tool in the overflow toolbar (shortcut `M`); clicking it, then an element/group, then placing points draws the path; Enter/double-click-near-last-point finalizes via the existing `actionFinalize` machinery.

**Editing** — `LinearElementEditor` surgically widened to support path point-dragging/midpoint-adding without touching its binding/arrowhead logic.

**Rendering** — dashed stroke + waypoint dots on canvas and in SVG export, distinguishing a path from a real line/arrow; restore.ts/bounds/collision support so paths survive scene restore and participate in hit-testing.

**Playback** — press-and-hold (~1s) on an element with an assigned path plays a fixed-speed (300px/s) animation along the path, reusing the existing shared `AnimationController`; the element snaps back to its original position at the end; re-triggering mid-animation is ignored; per-frame moves are explicitly marked non-undoable.

**Verification**: `yarn test:typecheck` clean, full `yarn test:update` run green (113 test files, 1531 tests passed, 0 failed).

Nothing has been committed — let me know if you'd like me to create a commit, or if you'd like to try it out in the dev server first.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-10-03 22:57:12Z)**_

Run `yarn start` from the repo root — it launches the `excalidraw-app` (excalidraw.com clone) dev server with Vite, hot-reloading, typically at `http://localhost:3000`.

Once it's running, here's the walkthrough for the feature:

1. **Create a target element** — draw any shape (rectangle, ellipse, etc.) on the canvas.
2. **Activate the Path tool** — click the "More tools" (overflow) dropdown at the end of the toolbar and pick **Motion path** (or press `M`).
3. **Pick the target** — click the shape you just drew. Nothing is created yet; the tool is now waiting for path points.
4. **Draw the path** — click to place a start point, click again for each additional waypoint (midpoints are optional), then finish by either pressing `Enter`, double-clicking, or clicking back near the last point.
5. **See it rendered** — the path shows as a dashed line with small dots at each waypoint, distinct from a regular line/arrow.
6. **Edit it** — with the path selected, double-click it (or press Enter) to re-enter point-editing mode: drag existing points, or double-click a segment to insert a midpoint.
7. **Play it back** — switch back to the Selection tool, then click-and-hold on the target shape for about a second. It should slide along the path at a constant speed and snap back to its original spot when it reaches the end.
8. **Multiple paths** — repeat steps 1–4 on a different shape to confirm two independent paths coexist and play back independently.

A couple of things worth watching for since this hasn't been manually driven yet:

- The overflow-dropdown placement for the tool (vs. a main-toolbar slot) — a UX call I made per the plan, happy to move it if it feels wrong.
- The dashed-line + dot visual treatment — easy to restyle if it doesn't read well against your canvas.

Want me to start the dev server now and drive it myself to confirm the flow works end-to-end, or would you rather try it yourself first?

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-10-03 23:34:41Z)**_

Found it. There's a condition in the pointerup handler that "commits" the in-progress point (letting a new one start) — it's gated by `isLinearElement`, which path intentionally isn't, so it silently never fires for paths. That's why points never freeze in place. Let me fix it.

```typescript
import React from "react";

import { KEYS, reseed } from "@excalidraw/common";

import type { ExcalidrawPathElement } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import { Excalidraw } from "../index";

import { act, render, fireEvent } from "./test-utils";

const { h } = window;

beforeEach(() => {
  localStorage.clear();
  reseed(7);
});

describe("path tool", () => {
  it("picks a target on first click, then draws and finalizes a multi-point path", async () => {
    const { getByToolName, container } = await render(<Excalidraw />);

    const canvas = container.querySelector("canvas.interactive")!;

    // draw a target rectangle
    const rectTool = getByToolName("rectangle");
    fireEvent.click(rectTool);
    fireEvent.pointerDown(canvas, { clientX: 20, clientY: 20 });
    fireEvent.pointerUp(canvas, { clientX: 120, clientY: 120 });

    expect(h.elements.length).toEqual(1);
    const rectangle = h.elements[0];

    // activate the path tool
    act(() => {
      h.app.setActiveTool({ type: "path" });
    });
    expect(h.state.activeTool.type).toEqual("path");

    // first click picks the target — no element created yet
    fireEvent.pointerDown(canvas, { clientX: 60, clientY: 60 });
    fireEvent.pointerUp(canvas, { clientX: 60, clientY: 60 });

    expect(h.elements.length).toEqual(1);
    expect(h.state.pendingPathTarget).toEqual({
      elementId: rectangle.id,
      groupId: null,
    });

    // second click places the first path point
    fireEvent.pointerDown(canvas, { clientX: 200, clientY: 200 });
    fireEvent.pointerUp(canvas, { clientX: 200, clientY: 200 });

    expect(h.state.pendingPathTarget).toBeNull();
    expect(h.state.multiElement).not.toBeNull();
    expect(h.state.multiElement?.type).toEqual("path");

    // move away, then click to commit the second point
    fireEvent.pointerMove(canvas, { clientX: 250, clientY: 260 });
    fireEvent.pointerDown(canvas, { clientX: 250, clientY: 260 });
    fireEvent.pointerUp(canvas);

    // move away, then click to commit the third point
    fireEvent.pointerMove(canvas, { clientX: 300, clientY: 340 });
    fireEvent.pointerDown(canvas);
    fireEvent.pointerUp(canvas);

    // finish via Enter
    fireEvent.keyDown(document, { key: KEYS.ENTER });

    expect(h.state.multiElement).toBeNull();
    expect(h.elements.length).toEqual(2);

    const path = h.elements.find(
      (el) => el.type === "path",
    ) as ExcalidrawPathElement;

    expect(path).toBeDefined();
    expect(path.targetElementId).toEqual(rectangle.id);
    expect(path.targetGroupId).toBeNull();
    expect(path.points.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3);
  });
});

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-10-04 00:23:17Z)**_

All clean. Here's what was wrong and what I fixed:

## Root cause (three compounding bugs)

1. **Target-pick hit-testing was too strict.** The first click (to pick the target element) used the same precise outline/fill hit-test as normal selection. A default rectangle has a transparent background, so clicking its _center_ never registered a hit — only clicking its border would. Fixed by hit-testing against the element's bounding box instead, which is what users intuitively expect for this interaction.
2. **The tool silently reverted to Selection after the first click.** A generic cleanup path resets `activeTool` back to the preferred selection tool whenever a click doesn't start a drag (correct for one-shot tools like rectangle, wrong for path's "pick target → draw points" two-phase flow). Added an explicit exception so the path tool manages its own tool-reset via its own finalize step.
3. **A duplicate point got baked in.** I had been promoting the path straight to `multiElement` on the same click that placed the first point; line/arrow instead promote on that click's _pointerup_, one tick later. The mismatch caused an extra `[0,0]` point to get committed. Fixed by matching line/arrow's timing exactly.

Along the way I also found and fixed a missing `"path"` case in `generateRoughOptions` (a runtime "Unimplemented type" crash during point-dragging) that TypeScript couldn't catch because that function takes an untyped `ExcalidrawElement`.

## Verification

- Added `packages/excalidraw/tests/pathElement.test.tsx`, a regression test driving the exact flow: create target → pick target → place 3 points → finalize by clicking back on the last point → assert the resulting `path` element's `targetElementId` and point count.
- Full suite: **114 test files, 1532 tests passed, 0 failed.** Typecheck clean.

Worth retesting in the dev server now — the original symptom (no visible points when drawing) should be resolved.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-10-04 00:33:34Z)**_

Same as before — from the repo root:

```
yarn start
```

This launches the `excalidraw-app` dev server (Vite + hot reload), typically at `http://localhost:3000`.

Walkthrough, now that the target-pick bug is fixed:

1. **Draw a target shape** — e.g. a rectangle, anywhere on the canvas. Leave it with its default transparent fill; clicking its center should now work for step 3.
2. **Open the Path tool** — click the "More tools" (⋯) dropdown at the end of the toolbar, pick **Motion path** (or press `M`).
3. **Click the shape** — anywhere inside its bounding box, not just its border. This picks it as the target; nothing is drawn yet.
4. **Place points** — click to drop a start point, move the mouse (you should now see a dashed rubber-band line following the cursor), click again for each additional waypoint.
5. **Finish the path** — either click back near the last point you placed, or double-click, or press Enter.
6. **Check the visual** — the path should render as a dashed line with small dots at each waypoint.
7. **Edit it** — select the path, double-click it (or press Enter while selected) to re-enter point-editing mode; drag a point, or double-click a segment to add a midpoint.
8. **Play it back** — switch to the Selection tool, then press-and-hold on the target shape for ~1 second. It should slide along the path and snap back to its start position.
9. **Multiple paths** — repeat on a second shape to confirm two paths coexist and animate independently.

Let me know what you find — especially if the rubber-band preview or the waypoint dots don't look right, since that's the part I verified only through the automated test, not a live render.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-10-04 00:45:07Z)**_

Thanks — these are three distinct, clear issues. Let me fix them.

**Issue 3 first (hidden points)** — this is a real rendering bug: when I widened the canvas-rendering code to treat `path` like line/arrow, I missed that the _generic bounding-box calculator_ still treats path elements as plain x/y/width/height boxes instead of computing bounds from their actual points. So when a later point goes further left/up than the first point, the computed bounding box is wrong and clips that content.

import { pointFrom, type LocalPoint } from "@excalidraw/math";
import { arrayToMap } from "@excalidraw/common";
import { API } from "@excalidraw/excalidraw/tests/helpers/api";

import { getElementAbsoluteCoords } from "../src/bounds";
import {
  getPathLength,
  getPathTargetElements,
  getPathsTargetingElement,
  getPointAtProgress,
} from "../src/path";

describe("path geometry helpers", () => {
  it("getPathLength sums segment distances", () => {
    const points: LocalPoint[] = [
      pointFrom(0, 0),
      pointFrom(30, 40), // 50
      pointFrom(30, 10), // 30
    ];
    expect(getPathLength(points)).toEqual(80);
  });

  it("getPointAtProgress interpolates along the ordered segments", () => {
    const points: LocalPoint[] = [pointFrom(0, 0), pointFrom(100, 0)];
    expect(getPointAtProgress(points, 0)).toEqual({ x: 0, y: 0 });
    expect(getPointAtProgress(points, 0.5)).toEqual({ x: 50, y: 0 });
    expect(getPointAtProgress(points, 1)).toEqual({ x: 100, y: 0 });
  });
});

describe("getElementAbsoluteCoords for path elements", () => {
  it("accounts for points extending left/above the first point (not clipped to x,y + width,height)", () => {
    // a point further left and above the first point — this previously fell
    // through to the generic x,y+width,height bounds calc (which assumes
    // element.x/y is always the top-left corner), hiding that portion of
    // the path
    const points: LocalPoint[] = [
      pointFrom(0, 0),
      pointFrom(-50, -40),
      pointFrom(20, 10),
    ];
    const element = API.createElement("path", {
      x: 200,
      y: 200,
      points,
    });
    const elementsMap = arrayToMap([element]);

    const [x1, y1, x2, y2] = getElementAbsoluteCoords(element, elementsMap);

    // the leftmost/topmost point is at local (-50,-40), so absolute bounds
    // must extend to (200-50, 200-40), not stop at element.x/y
    expect(x1).toEqual(150);
    expect(y1).toEqual(160);
    expect(x2).toEqual(220);
    expect(y2).toEqual(210);
  });
});

describe("getPathTargetElements / getPathsTargetingElement", () => {
  it("resolves a single-element target and its reverse lookup", () => {
    const rectangle = API.createElement("rectangle", { x: 0, y: 0, size: 50 });
    const path = API.createElement("path", {
      x: 100,
      y: 100,
      points: [pointFrom(0, 0), pointFrom(50, 50)],
      targetElementId: rectangle.id,
    });
    const elements = [rectangle, path];

    expect(getPathTargetElements(path, elements)).toEqual([rectangle]);
    expect(getPathsTargetingElement(rectangle, elements)).toEqual([path]);
  });

  it("returns an empty array once the target is deleted", () => {
    const rectangle = API.createElement("rectangle", {
      x: 0,
      y: 0,
      size: 50,
      isDeleted: true,
    });
    const path = API.createElement("path", {
      x: 100,
      y: 100,
      points: [pointFrom(0, 0), pointFrom(50, 50)],
      targetElementId: rectangle.id,
    });

    expect(getPathTargetElements(path, [rectangle, path])).toEqual([]);
  });
});

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-10-04 01:05:40Z)**_

All green. Here's a summary of the three fixes from your dev-server test:

1. **Path no longer re-enters edit mode after confirm.** Removed the `LinearElementEditor` selection state for finished paths in both finalize code paths (click-to-finish and Enter/Escape-to-finish), and reverted the `actionToggleLinearEditor` predicate so double-click/Enter never re-opens point editing for a path. Line/arrow are unaffected.

2. **The shape now visually locks onto the drawn path.** The playback math previously only replayed the path's _shape_ as an offset from the target's own current position — it never accounted for where the path actually sits on the canvas, so the element moved in the right pattern but never touched the dashed line. Fixed by computing a one-time alignment at the start of playback that snaps the target's bounding-box center onto the path's first point (in absolute scene coordinates), then displaces it by the path's shape from there — so it now rides the literal drawn line.

3. **Points above/left of the first point are no longer hidden** — a real bug. Path elements were falling through to a generic "x,y + width,height" bounding-box calculation that assumes the element's origin is always the top-left corner. For a path, if a later point goes further up or left than the first point, that assumption breaks and clips the canvas. Fixed by routing path elements through the same points-aware bounds calculation line/arrow already use.

Added a unit test locking in the bounds fix (`packages/element/tests/path.test.ts`) and updated the end-to-end regression test to assert paths aren't re-editable. Full suite: 115 files, 1537 passed, typecheck clean.

Worth another dev-server pass on all three, especially #2 since it's the most visually subjective — let me know if the "lock-on" point (bounding-box center) feels right or if you'd expect a different anchor (e.g., top-left corner).

11:} from "@excalidraw/element/types";

13:import { AnimationController } from "./renderer/animation";

15:import type App from "./components/App";
16:
17:/** constant speed, not fixed duration — longer paths naturally take longer */
18:const PATH_PLAYBACK_SPEED_PX_PER_SEC = 300;
19:
20:type PlaybackState = {
21:  elapsed: number;
22:  totalDuration: number;
23:  originalPositions: Map<string, { x: number; y: number }>;
24:};
25:
26:/**
27: * Drives the basic, fixed-speed "press and hold to preview" path animation.
28: * Reuses the shared `AnimationController` (a single RAF loop multiplexing
29: * every concurrently-keyed animation) rather than running its own loop, so
30: * multiple paths can play back at once with no extra scheduling code.
31: *
32: * The target's combined bounding-box center is locked onto the path: at the
33: * start of playback it's aligned exactly onto the path's first point (in
34: * absolute scene coordinates), and from there it's displaced by however much
35: * the path's shape moves at progress `t` — so the target visibly rides the
36: * drawn dashed line rather than merely replaying its shape from wherever the
37: * target happens to currently sit.
38: *
39: * Per-frame mutations are explicitly scheduled as `CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER`
40: * on every tick (not left to the default `EVENTUALLY`), since an animation
41: * can run for seconds, during which an unrelated user action could schedule
42: * an `IMMEDIATELY` capture that would otherwise sweep a mid-flight frame into
43: * an unrelated undo entry.
44: */
45:export class PathPlaybackController {
46:  constructor(private app: App) {}
47:
48:  isPlaying(path: ExcalidrawPathElement): boolean {
49:    return AnimationController.running(playbackKey(path.id));
50:  }
51:
52:  start(path: ExcalidrawPathElement, targets: NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[]) {
53:    const key = playbackKey(path.id);
54:
55:    if (AnimationController.running(key) || targets.length === 0) {
56:      return;
57:    }
58:
59:    const length = getPathLength(path.points);
60:    const totalDuration = Math.max(
61:      (length / PATH_PLAYBACK_SPEED_PX_PER_SEC) * 1000,
62:      1,
63:    );
64:
65:    const elementsMap = this.app.scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap();
66:    const originalPositions = new Map<string, { x: number; y: number }>();
67:    for (const target of targets) {
68:      originalPositions.set(target.id, { x: target.x, y: target.y });
69:      const boundText = getBoundTextElement(target, elementsMap);
70:      if (boundText) {
71:        originalPositions.set(boundText.id, {
72:          x: boundText.x,
73:          y: boundText.y,
74:        });
75:      }
76:    }
77:
78:    // one-time alignment so the target's combined bounding-box center lands
79:    // exactly on the path's first point (in absolute scene coordinates) at
80:    // t=0, then stays glued to the path's shape as it progresses — without
81:    // this, the target would only replay the path's shape as an offset from
82:    // its own current position, never visually touching the drawn line
83:    const [minX, minY, maxX, maxY] = getCommonBounds(targets, elementsMap);
84:    const referenceCenter = { x: (minX + maxX) / 2, y: (minY + maxY) / 2 };
85:    const [startLocalX, startLocalY] = path.points[0] ?? [0, 0];
86:    const pathStartAbs = {
87:      x: path.x + startLocalX,
88:      y: path.y + startLocalY,
89:    };
90:    const alignmentOffset = {
91:      x: pathStartAbs.x - referenceCenter.x,
92:      y: pathStartAbs.y - referenceCenter.y,
93:    };
94:
95:    AnimationController.start<PlaybackState>(key, ({ deltaTime, state }) => {
96:      const next: PlaybackState = state
97:        ? { ...state, elapsed: state.elapsed + deltaTime }
98:        : { elapsed: 0, totalDuration, originalPositions };
99:
100:      const t = Math.min(next.elapsed / next.totalDuration, 1);
101:      const { x: dx, y: dy } = getPointAtProgress(path.points, t);
102:      const [startDx, startDy] = path.points[0] ?? [0, 0];
103:      const totalDeltaX = dx - startDx + alignmentOffset.x;
104:      const totalDeltaY = dy - startDy + alignmentOffset.y;
105:
106:      const liveOriginalPositions = new Map(
107:        [...next.originalPositions].filter(([id]) =>
108:          this.app.scene.getNonDeletedElement(id),
109:        ),
110:      );
111:
112:      if (liveOriginalPositions.size === 0) {
113:        return null;
114:      }
115:
116:      for (const [id, orig] of liveOriginalPositions) {
117:        const element = this.app.scene.getNonDeletedElement(id);
118:        if (!element) {
119:          continue;
120:        }
121:        this.app.scene.mutateElement(
122:          element,
123:          {
124:            x: orig.x + totalDeltaX,
125:            y: orig.y + totalDeltaY,
126:          },
127:          { informMutation: true, isDragging: true },
128:        );
129:      }
130:      this.app.scheduleNeverCapture();
131:
132:      if (t >= 1) {
133:        for (const [id, orig] of liveOriginalPositions) {
134:          const element = this.app.scene.getNonDeletedElement(id);
135:          if (element) {
136:            this.app.scene.mutateElement(element, orig, {
137:              informMutation: true,
138:              isDragging: false,
139:            });
140:          }
141:        }
142:        this.app.scheduleNeverCapture();
143:        return null;
144:      }
145:
146:      return next;
147:    });
148:  }
149:
150:  cancel(path: ExcalidrawPathElement) {
151:    AnimationController.cancel(playbackKey(path.id));
152:  }
153:}
154:
155:const playbackKey = (pathId: string) => `path-playback-${pathId}`;

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-10-04 01:35:22Z)**_

Clean. Here's what changed for the two issues you found:

**1. Rotation disabled for paths.** Added `path` alongside `frame` in the transform-handle logic that omits the rotation handle — same exact mechanism frames already use. Since a path's points are read directly in its own local (unrotated) coordinate space for both rendering and the snap/playback math, letting it rotate would desync the visual line from where the shape actually goes. Now there's simply no rotate handle on a selected path.

**2. Target now snapped to the path at rest, not just during playback.** Previously the target only aligned onto the path's absolute position _during_ an animation, returning to its original (unrelated) position afterward. Now, the moment a path is confirmed, the target is permanently repositioned so its bounding-box center sits exactly on the path's first point — snapped together at rest. I factored the alignment math into a shared `getPathAlignmentOffset` helper used both at confirm-time (one-time repositioning) and at playback-start (a now-usually-no-op safety net for if the path or target gets moved later). Since playback still returns to the target's position at animation start, and that position is now the snapped one, the resting state after playback stays snapped too.

Verified with new unit tests (`getPathAlignmentOffset`, no-rotation-handle check) and an updated end-to-end test asserting the rectangle's center lands exactly on the path's start after confirm. Full suite: 115 files, 1540 passed, typecheck clean.

Worth another dev-server pass — particularly checking that resize (not rotate) still behaves reasonably on a path, since I left that alone.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-10-04 01:58:34Z)**_

Clean. Here's what changed for this round:

**Path and target now drag together.** Previously `dragSelectedElements` (the shared drag-move logic) only pulled a frame's children along when dragging a frame — nothing analogous existed for a path/target pair, so dragging either one left the other behind, breaking the snap. I extended that same mechanism: when the drag selection includes a path, its resolved target(s) are pulled in; when it includes an element that's the target of some path(s), those path(s) are pulled in too. Both directions now move together by the identical offset, using the existing per-element update logic unchanged (no path-specific drawing code needed there).

Verified with two new end-to-end tests — dragging the rectangle moves the path, and dragging the path moves the rectangle — plus the full suite: 115 files, 1542 passed, typecheck clean.

One thing worth you checking in the dev server: I didn't touch _resize_ (only drag/translate), so resizing the target or the path independently will still desync them — let me know if that also needs to pull both together, or if it's fine for now since you only mentioned dragging.

279	): TransformHandles => {
280	  // so that when locked element is selected (especially when you toggle lock
281	  // via keyboard) the locked element is visually distinct, indicating
282	  // you can't move/resize
283	  if (
284	    element.locked ||
285	    // Elbow arrows cannot be rotated
286	    isElbowArrow(element)
287	  ) {
288	    return {};
289	  }
290
291	  if (element.type === "freedraw" || isLinearElement(element)) {
292	    if (element.points.length === 2) {
293	      // only check the last point because starting point is always (0,0)
294	      const [, p1] = element.points;
295	      if (p1[0] === 0 || p1[1] === 0) {
296	        omitSides = OMIT_SIDES_FOR_LINE_BACKSLASH;
297	      } else if (p1[0] > 0 && p1[1] < 0) {
298	        omitSides = OMIT_SIDES_FOR_LINE_SLASH;
299	      } else if (p1[0] > 0 && p1[1] > 0) {
300	        omitSides = OMIT_SIDES_FOR_LINE_BACKSLASH;
301	      } else if (p1[0] < 0 && p1[1] > 0) {
302	        omitSides = OMIT_SIDES_FOR_LINE_SLASH;
303	      } else if (p1[0] < 0 && p1[1] < 0) {
304	        omitSides = OMIT_SIDES_FOR_LINE_BACKSLASH;
305	      }
306	    }
307	  } else if (isFrameLikeElement(element) || isPathElement(element)) {
308	    // a path's points are drawn in its own local (unrotated) coordinate
309	    // space, and playback/snap-to-path positioning reads them directly —
310	    // rotating the path would desync the visual line from that math, so
311	    // rotation is disabled entirely rather than kept in sync
312	    omitSides = {
313	      ...omitSides,
314	      rotation: true,
315	    };
316	  }
317	  const margin = isLinearElement(element)
318	    ? DEFAULT_TRANSFORM_HANDLE_SPACING + 8
319	    : isImageElement(element)
320	    ? 0
321	    : DEFAULT_TRANSFORM_HANDLE_SPACING;
322	  return getTransformHandlesFromCoords(
323	    getElementAbsoluteCoords(element, elementsMap, true),
324	    element.angle,
325	    zoom,
326	    pointerType,
327	    omitSides,
328	    margin,
329	    isImageElement(element) ? 0 : undefined,
330	  );
331	};
```

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-10-04 02:47:28Z)**_

Clean. Found and fixed the actual culprit: there's a _second_, independent resize mechanism (`resizeTest`'s "resize from sides" fallback in `resizeTest.ts`) that hit-tests the bounding-box edges directly via line-segment proximity — it doesn't go through `getTransformHandles` at all, so disabling the drawn handles earlier didn't touch it. That's exactly what let clicking the boundary line (not a handle) trigger an axis-constrained resize that looked like horizontal/vertical "sliding."

Added an early `return false` for path elements at the top of `resizeTest`, so paths can no longer be resized via drawn handles _or_ via a direct boundary-edge grab — only moved by dragging the body (which still pulls the target along). Covered with a new unit test that clicks directly on a path's bounding-box edge and confirms no handle type resolves. Full suite: 115 files, 1543 passed, typecheck clean.

Commit the motion path feature

```bash
cd "C:\Users\tonyw\projects\draw_main_proj\excalidraw" && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
feat: add motion path tool (#45)

Adds a new first-class "path" element type for defining a motion
trajectory that a selected element or group can follow, per issue #45
(head issue #18).

- Path tool: click a target element/group, then click to place a
  start point, optional midpoints, and an end point; finish by
  clicking back near the last point or pressing Enter/Escape. Reuses
  the existing multi-point line drawing/editing machinery.
- Points-only editing during creation; a path is intentionally not
  re-editable, resizable, or rotatable after confirm, since its
  points, the snap-to-target alignment, and playback math all read
  directly from its unrotated local points/x/y.
- On confirm, the target is snapped so its bounding-box center sits
  on the path's start point, and dragging either the path or its
  target moves both together, keeping them visually coincident at
  rest and not just mid-animation.
- Press-and-hold (~1s) on the target plays a fixed-speed animation
  along the path via the existing shared AnimationController, with
  the target snapping back to its resting position afterward;
  concurrent paths on different targets animate independently.
- Dashed-line + waypoint-dot rendering on canvas and in SVG export;
  restore/bounds/collision support so paths persist and hit-test
  correctly, including when later points extend above/left of the
  path's start.

Covered by new unit and end-to-end tests in
packages/element/tests/path.test.ts and
packages/excalidraw/tests/pathElement.test.tsx.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
```
